# dsh-math-literal

Keeps single-`$` dollars literal in DeepSeek Harness web chat.

The web chat renders a message with two markdown grammars: while it streams,
a math-free grammar; once it settles, a grammar with single-`$` inline math
enabled. So prose like

> paired: from $55,011 outgoing rollover to $230 contributions

streams correctly, then — at settle — the two `$` are read as an inline-math
pair and everything between them is run through KaTeX:

> paired: from 55,011outgoingrolloverato230 contributions

For a coding harness, `$HOME`, `$DSH_*` and currency are far more common in
model prose than inline TeX, so that default is backwards. This plugin turns
every lone `$` into an escaped `\$` at render time, which both grammars render
as a literal dollar sign — so the settled view matches the streaming view,
and **real math keeps working**: `$$x^2$$`, `$$` blocks, `\(x^2\)`, `\[ … \]`
pass through untouched, and `$` inside code spans and code blocks stays
byte-for-byte verbatim.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-math-literal-v<version>&path:/packages/math-literal"
```

If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-math-literal-v<version>&path:/packages/math-literal"
```

…then add `dsh-math-literal` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`.

> **Warning:** never install this plugin by bare name (`pnpm add
> dsh-math-literal`): an unscoped `dsh-*` name on the npm registry can belong
> to an unrelated author. Always use the git-tag spec above.

Restart dsh. There is nothing to configure.

## What it does, and how

- **Host half** (`src/host.mjs`): subscribes to the `webserver/index-inject`
  event (the same seam `dsh-client-shortcuts` uses) and pushes one head
  `<script>` into every index response. The script
  (`src/wrapper.mjs`, a reviewed, readable IIFE — not minified) intercepts
  `window.__ModuleLoader__.create` before the shell's boot kernel calls it and
  replaces the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` entry of the static
  module table — the frozen namespace object every `MarkdownText` consumer
  reads from — with a plain copy whose `MarkdownText` runs `text` through
  `globalThis.__DSH_MATH_LITERAL_ESCAPE__` before rendering. Ordering-robust
  (the boot queue facade may or may not exist yet) and idempotent.
- **Client half** (`src/client.mjs`, `dsh.client.immediately: true` so it is
  prefetched in the shell's immediate boot tier): loads the package-local
  chunk `src/client.parser.js` and installs the escape function as that
  global. The escape (`src/escape.mjs`) fast-paths text without `$`;
  otherwise it parses with a commonmark-only `fromMarkdown` to locate every
  code region, then one pass: skip code, keep `$$` pairs, keep already
  escaped `\$`, escape every other `$`.
- The stored session log and the model's context are **untouched** — this is
  a render-time transform only.

| Input | After transform | Renders as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$55,011 … $230` | `\$55,011 … \$230` | literal — both arms agree |
| `$$x^2$$`, `$$` blocks, `\(x^2\)`, `\[ … \]` | unchanged | math (unchanged KaTeX path, copy-tex intact) |
| `\$` (already escaped) | unchanged | literal `$` |
| `$` in fenced / indented / inline code | unchanged | verbatim code |

## Configuration

None. Disabling the plugin means removing its row (or disabling it in
Settings); the page then boots exactly as it did before the plugin existed.
Nothing is left half-active.

## Failure modes

- **Frontend architecture drift.** The wrapper targets the seed-table words
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` and `react/jsx-runtime` and the
  `__ModuleLoader__.create` choke point. If a future shell changes any of
  them, the wrapper's feature detection simply does not fire (one
  `console.warn`, no crash) and the plugin degrades to the pre-plugin
  behavior — the page never fails to boot because of it.
- **Parser chunk fails to load** (network, route change): the escape global
  stays unset, the wrapper renders the original text. Same degradation, one
  `console.warn`.
- **The escape throws on some input**: caught per render; that render uses
  the original text.
- **Cost**: one extra markdown parse for each rendered message *containing*
  `$` (the common dollar-free case is a single `includes` check).

## The generated parser chunk

`src/client.parser.js` is a generated artifact (banner included): an IIFE
bundle of `mdast-util-from-markdown` plus `src/escape.mjs` embedded verbatim,
registered as a package-local client chunk. Rebuild it (from this package's
root, with the devDependencies installed) when bumping the parser:

```sh
npm install --no-save --no-package-lock
node scripts/build-parser.mjs
```

`test/chunk.test.mjs` pins the embedded escape source and the parser-version
banner, so a stale artifact fails the test suite instead of shipping.

## Upstream

The shipped frontend build hard-wires the math extension's
`singleDollarTextMath` option to `true` (the option works upstream; the
bundled vendor chunk drops it). An upstream fix — passing
`singleDollarTextMath: false`, or exposing it — would make this plugin
removable: drop the bundle row, and nothing else changes.

# dsh-model-capacity

**Process-wide, per-provider model-call capacity for DeepSeek Harness.**

One host plugin gates every `ctx.llm.stream()` call — interactive turns, subagent
children, judges, titles and compaction — with a per-provider counting semaphore.
Every call waits in the same strict FIFO queue for its provider, in arrival
order, whoever started it. The Host exposes a Capacity panel with active leases
and queued calls.

Nothing here is per-session or per-browser. It is one service in the DSH host
process, shared by all sessions.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-capacity-v<version>&path:/packages/model-capacity"
```

Or add the same git spec to the profile's `package.json` and list
`dsh-model-capacity` in `dsh.profile.bundles`. The bundle mounts row
`id: model-capacity`. The row carries **no config**; write the complete section
in your own profile patch (a patch layer replaces a row's whole `config`).

## Config

```yaml
- id: model-capacity
  config:
    enabled: true
    defaultMaxConcurrent: 1
    limits:
      - provider: gpu-a
        maxConcurrent: 2
      - provider: gpu-b
        maxConcurrent: 2
      - provider: cloud-proxy
        unlimited: true
    queueLimitPerProvider: 1000
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | `false` makes the gate inert while keeping the panel available. |
| `defaultMaxConcurrent` | Limit for a provider with no `limits` entry. Unknown providers therefore admit one call at a time. |
| `limits[]` | `{provider, maxConcurrent}` or `{provider, unlimited: true}`. Capacity is **per provider**, because a provider is the physical backend a deployment split its GPUs into. Every model id behind one provider shares its slots. `unlimited: true` means no queue and no rejection for that route (intended for a cloud proxy). |
| `queueLimitPerProvider` | Bound on queued calls per provider; exceeding it rejects new calls with `CAPACITY_QUEUE_FULL` instead of growing memory forever. |

`reservationTtlMs` and `subagentTools` were config keys up to and including 0.3.0.
They are gone: a deployment that still carries them boots with one
`unknown config key "…" (ignored)` warning per key.

Every provider named in `limits` has a visible queue even at `0/limit`, and the
deployment's default model provider is seeded the same way; other providers
appear on first use. Adding both of your provider routes to `limits` is the
simplest way to see two queues in the panel.

Limits are validated against `ctx.llm.listProviders()` when adapters register; a
limit naming a route the host never offers is logged loudly (the configured limit
still applies if it appears). The config is watched through the host
`configEditor` and swapped atomically; an invalid reload keeps the previous
limits.

The Activity page's **Adjust limits** dialog edits these fields directly. Saving
writes the complete limits section back through `configEditor.edit`, applies the
new manager limits immediately, and persists the change in the profile YAML.

## Behavior

| Caller | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Ordinary prompt / any session model call | `llm/stream` waits for a slot before the adapter sees the request. The session stays `running`; the composer dock shows position, provider/model and elapsed time, with **Cancel turn**. There is no plugin-level timeout. |
| `subagent` / `subagent_fork` / `spawn_teammate` / `workflow` | No special path. A dispatch is never refused for capacity: the child's own calls go through the same global gate and queue FIFO behind whatever is already waiting for that provider. The parent sees the tool as running for the child's whole wait-plus-run time. |
| Kanban | Uses the same global gate per call. It no longer owns a semaphore, leases or capacity checks; `wipCap` only bounds how many tickets are in `Now`. |

`unlimited: true` providers never enter the FIFO; the panel labels them
`unlimited`.

Because the wait happens **before** `next()` reaches the provider adapter, the
provider's `streamIdleTimeoutMs` does not start until a slot exists.

### Why the subagent preflight was removed

Up to 0.3.0 an agent-spawning tool asked for a slot before its child existed,
returned a model-visible capacity error when the provider was full, and handed
that reservation to the child's first call. It cost a synchronous guess at the
child's route, a TTL timer for reservations whose child never arrived, and a
second admission path that could jump the queue this gate exists to enforce.

A dispatch is not an inference call. What is being protected is the hardware
behind a provider route, and every request that reaches it already passes
through this gate — a subagent child's included. So the gate is the whole
mechanism: nothing holds a slot unless a stream is live, and one queue orders
everything. The trade is that a busy provider no longer tells the model "do not
bother dispatching"; the child simply waits, visibly, in the same queue.

### Session-log wait history

Every queued main call that waited more than 250 ms is recorded in memory with
its provider, model, turn number and duration. A `conversation.chat.turnTail`
entry renders those waits beneath the turn in the chat log as a small collapsible
card:

```
Waited for capacity  24s  1 wait
  local-ai-machine (apu)/medium-dense        24s
```

This is client-only and never written to the session log or model context, so it
does not perturb the conversation. The history is per host process (a restart
clears it) and covers main calls only; title/compaction waits and judge calls are
not recorded.

### Composer dock width

The queued-session banner uses the same width calculation as the core composer
dock (`--dsh-composer-side-clearance` / `--dsh-composer-card-max-width`), so it
aligns with the message column instead of spanning the full viewport. This is what
makes multi-hour waits safe for a machine that thinks for hours.

The gate is in-process: a host restart clears all leases and waiters (their turns
are already interrupted by the restart). No database is used.

## Panel

- The **Activity** sidebar entry carries one tiny round pill per provider in
  real time, rendered after the word `Capacity`. The left number is **active +
  queued** demand, so a full provider with one call waiting reads `3/2`; an
  unlimited provider reads `3/∞`. Pills use a light tinted fill with a darker
  border and text: green while there is free capacity, yellow when exactly at
  capacity, red when anything is queued. Hovering a pill names the provider
  (`local-ai-machine (apu): 3/2 · 2 active · 1 queued`). The collapsed rail hides
  the pills because the 36 px rail cannot fit them without overlapping the icon.
- `sidebar.panellist` entry **Activity** → a Context-tab-like full page: header
  with live enforcing status, KPI cards (active / queued), and one
  colour-accented card per provider with a capacity bar. Each active or queued
  call is a session card showing title, workspace, model, kind and elapsed/waited
  time. **Click any session card to open that session**; active cards breathe with
  a green glow. The page uses the
  same card/hover language as `dsh-context`'s Context overview. Session titles come from
  the session log's `title` projection; workspace names come from the workspace
  registry, matched by the session's cwd.
- The Activity page animates handover, because a list that silently re-shuffles is
  unreadable. Each poll diffs a provider against the one before it: a lease that
  left Active is re-rendered in its old position as an inert ghost clone that
  scales up and fades out (~350 ms); a session that moved from Queue to Active gets
  a slide-down-and-fade entrance; the cards still queued slide up to close the gap
  (a small in-section FLIP on `leaseId`/`waiterId` keys, so the motion follows the
  card, not the row). The panel polls every 750 ms so this lands while you are
  looking at it. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` none of it runs — no ghost is even
  mounted, and the lists simply update.
- `conversation.input.dock` on every session: appears only while that session has
  a queued call.
- Controls: **Cancel turn** (safe; cancels the session's active turn, which
  aborts the waiter), **Cancel** a queued call, and
  **Force release** a lease behind a confirmation (the underlying stream may
  still run; this can exceed the limit — use it only for a stuck lease).

Routes are under the authenticated `/api` fence:
`/api/modelCapacity/{snapshot,cancelSession,cancelWaiter,forceRelease}`.

## Tests

```sh
node --test test/*.test.mjs
```

Covers FIFO admission, abort/cancel, force-release, raising limits, the queue
bound, the `llm/stream` gate (acquire before the first chunk, release on
abort/error, and a subagent child queued strictly in arrival order behind an
interactive call), config resolution including the removed 0.3.0 keys, and host
contracts (no tool registration, no tool guard, no credentials, routes under
`/api`).

The browser half is not unit-tested and deliberately stays that way: `src/client.mjs`
is a classic script for `window.__ModuleLoader__` with no module boundary to import
through, so a test would mean extracting the diff into a second file that only the
browser loads — a seam for no reviewer's benefit. What it does get is the repository's
Rules-of-Hooks gate (`node scripts/check-plugin-hooks.mjs`, the only automated check
that can see this file at all) plus the deployment's lab UI smoke, which mounts the
panel for real and fails on any `slot entry crashed`. The animation behaviour itself is
listed above and verified by eye against live traffic.

# dsh-plugins

Public [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins by [Chris Johnson](https://github.com/chrisjohnson). One repository, independently installable plugins — each with its own README, its own tests, its own changelog and its own version.

## Install

**Nothing here is published to npm.** Every release is a git tag on this repository, named `<package>-v<version>` (for example `dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1`), and you install a plugin by pinning that tag plus the package's subdirectory:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

`dsh plugin add` hands that spec to pnpm and also lists the package under the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, which is what activates its configuration layer. If you manage a profile's `package.json` yourself, the same spec works with pnpm directly — but then add the package name to `dsh.profile.bundles` by hand, because a plain `pnpm add` installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

Pick the tag from [the repository's tags](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags); `<dir>` is the folder under `packages/` in the index below.

> **Warning — do not install these by bare name.** `pnpm add dsh-model-switch` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-model-switch`) resolves against the npm registry, and the npm package called `dsh-model-switch` belongs to an unrelated author: it is **not** this plugin. The same can happen to any unscoped `dsh-*` name. Always use the git-tag spec above.

## Index

| Plugin | What it is for | Latest | Directory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **[dsh-model-switch](./packages/model-switch/)** | Let the agent switch its own model mid-session, with a context-window fit guard so neither it nor a human in the composer can strand a conversation on a model too small to read it. | 0.2.1 | `packages/model-switch` |
| **[dsh-image-search-searxng](./packages/image-search-searxng/)** | A model-facing `image_search` tool over your own SearXNG, rendered inline in the Web GUI. | 0.2.0 | `packages/image-search-searxng` |
| **[dsh-continue-kicker](./packages/continue-kicker/)** | Automatically send "continue" when a turn halts on the output-token limit (or after a crash, or on a reasoning-only empty stop), with a runaway guard that stops after repeated kicks with no progress. | 0.2.0 | `packages/continue-kicker` |
| **[dsh-loop-watchdog](./packages/loop-watchdog/)** | Detect an agent stuck in a loop before each step (a deterministic repetition check plus an optional model judge), keep an audit ledger of every check, optionally steer the session, and chart the ledger in a `dsh-better-sidebar` panel. | 0.1.0 | `packages/loop-watchdog` |
| **[dsh-scheduled-queue](./packages/scheduled-queue/)** | Schedule the composer's draft to be sent to its own session later, with a per-session dock to edit, cancel or send now. Runs alongside the official schedule bundle. | 0.1.0 | `packages/scheduled-queue` |
| **[dsh-kanban](./packages/kanban/)** | Ticket-centric work organizer and code-driven workflow engine: a local SQLite board whose phases spawn sandboxed role sessions, gate on per-provider capacity, verify machine-readable conditions, and record a complete time/token ledger. | 0.1.0 | `packages/kanban` |
| **[dsh-model-capacity](./packages/model-capacity/)** | Process-wide, per-provider model-call capacity: every call — an interactive turn or a subagent child's — queues FIFO for its provider, and a panel inspects active leases and waiters. | 0.4.0 | `packages/model-capacity` |
| **[dsh-better-git-worktree](./packages/better-git-worktree/)** | Run a session in its own self-contained git working copy: a composer Worktree switch, a `worktree_convert` tool, session-list status badges, a header menu, and an archive prompt that decides the working copy's fate. | 0.1.1 | `packages/better-git-worktree` |
| **[dsh-session-cost](./packages/session-cost/)** | A compact estimated-cost badge in the composer stats bar: reads the session billed-token buckets and prices them with public models.dev rates, hidden at $0. | 0.1.0 | `packages/session-cost` |
| **[dsh-math-literal](./packages/math-literal/)** | Keeps single-`$` dollars literal in web chat: unpaired `$` in settled markdown renders as a literal dollar sign (matching the streaming arm) instead of opening an inline-math pair, while real math and code regions are untouched. | 0.1.0 | `packages/math-literal` |
| **[dsh-browser](./packages/browser/)** | One browser context per DSH session on a single shared remote Browserless connection for `dsh-playwright-browser`'s tools, with reconnect after a dropped connection, context cleanup when a session ends, and an announced local fallback. | 0.1.0 | `packages/browser` |

Install lines for the latest release of each package:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1&path:/packages/model-switch"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-image-search-searxng-v0.2.0&path:/packages/image-search-searxng"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-continue-kicker-v0.2.0&path:/packages/continue-kicker"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-loop-watchdog-v0.1.0&path:/packages/loop-watchdog"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-scheduled-queue-v0.1.0&path:/packages/scheduled-queue"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-kanban-v0.1.0&path:/packages/kanban"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-capacity-v0.4.0&path:/packages/model-capacity"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-better-git-worktree-v0.1.1&path:/packages/better-git-worktree"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-session-cost-v0.1.0&path:/packages/session-cost"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-math-literal-v0.1.0&path:/packages/math-literal"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-browser-v0.1.0&path:/packages/browser"
```

Each package's README is the contract: what it does, every configuration key and what happens when it is unset, how it fails, how to install it, and how to run its checks. Nothing important lives only here.

## Releases

1. A release is a normal pull request that bumps one package's version and moves its CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry under that version.
2. After it merges, the tag `<package>-v<version>` is cut on that merge commit and pushed. Nothing is committed directly to `main`.
3. Consumers pin the tag with the install spec above. A tag is never moved or rewritten once pushed.

Details: [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## What "a plugin from this repo" means

- **Plain ESM, no build step.** `git clone && npm test` works with nothing installed. No bundler, no TypeScript layer, no generated client — what the harness loads is what is in `src/`.
- **Every plugin declares `dsh.bundle.patch`**, so one command installs *and* activates it; nothing here needs a hand-edited `cordis.yml`.
- **Deployment-specific values are configuration, never defaults.** A plugin that "works on my machine" because it hard-codes my provider ids is broken for everyone else. `node scripts/verify.mjs` fails the build on author-local paths and provider ids.
- **Nothing is required to be configured.** Optional features report themselves unavailable and name the key that enables them, instead of throwing at boot or failing at first use.
- **Every decision worth testing lives in a module that imports nothing from dsh**, which is what makes the tests real rather than decorative.

## Checking this repository

```sh
npm run check          # verify + hook gate + all tests, no install needed
node scripts/verify.mjs            # the release contract (see below)
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs     # install into a throwaway profile, import, compose
```

`scripts/verify.mjs` is the interesting one: it enforces the rules that make a plugin installable and trustworthy — `dsh.bundle.patch` present and loading the package by name, `dsh.client` matched by an `./client` export, one harness peer range across every package (`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`; dsh checks it with prereleases included, while plain node-semver/pnpm admit only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases from it), every shipped file inside the `files` allowlist (all a git-tag install ships), a git-tag install line (and no bare-name one) in every package README, every config key documented in its README, every package listed in the index above, and no deployment leakage. It runs on CI for every push and it runs on a bare clone.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). If you are an agent working in this repository, read [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) first; it is short and it exists because these plugins run with your user's credentials.

For how these plugins get developed, tested against a live harness, released and consumed by the deployment they came from, see [docs/testing.md](./docs/testing.md) and [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

# dsh-model-switch

**Let the agent change its own model mid-session — and make it impossible to strand the conversation on a model too small to read it.**

Two tools and two interface surfaces for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), built for deployments that route the same session across models with wildly different context windows (a 1M-token cloud route and a 262k local one, say):

| What | Who | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `switch_model` tool | agent | Moves this session to `provider/model` and sends it a self-contained handoff message. Full history carries over. |
| `switch_model_escalate` tool | agent | "I'm stuck" escape hatch to a route **you** designate. The model does not choose the destination — deployment policy does. |
| Context badge | human | Appears beside the composer's model picker the moment the routed model cannot hold the session — amber `210k / 262.1k — compacts at 209.7k`, or red `300k > 262.1k — won't fit`. Its tooltip lists the routes that still fit, and clicking it is how you open the repair panel below. |
| Repair panel | human | Collapsed by default, because past the auto-compact line nothing fails: the next request compacts on the route that can still read it. Click the badge for one-click repair — move to a route that can read the transcript, compact there, return. The one case that cannot wait for a click (past the route's own window, where the next request 400s and overflow recovery summarises with the route that just overflowed) opens itself once. |

The guard applies to the agent's tools **and** the human's picker. It has to be in both places, for a reason that is not obvious: the composer calls `sessionController.selectModel` directly and cannot be intercepted, so the interactive path is warned-and-repaired rather than blocked.

## Why this exists

A real session, 2026-09-28. It had run to ~421k tokens on a route with a 1,048,576-token window. The user switched it to a local model with a 262,144-token window and sent one message:

```
attempt 1  → Request timed out.
attempt 2  → 400 ContextWindowExceededError: request (420948 tokens)
             exceeds the available context size (262144 tokens)
compaction/start   ← the harness classified it and started overflow recovery
compaction/end     ← error: the same 400, at 421,300 tokens
retry              → same 400 → surfaced to the user
```

Two harness behaviours combine to make that unrecoverable:

1. The pre-step pressure gate resolves its target from the **last minted request**, which right after a switch is still the *old* model — so the threshold it compares against is 0.8 × 1,048,576, nothing compacts, and the first request on the new, smaller route is structurally unguarded.
2. Overflow recovery summarizes with the **route that just overflowed**. The rescue call had to push 421k tokens through a 262k model.

A model must *read* a conversation in order to summarize it. That is a physical ceiling, not a tuning problem: the only moment a 421k session can be condensed is while a big-window model is still routed. Hence the rule this plugin enforces — **compact to fit before switching, and refuse with actionable numbers when even that is impossible.**

Every number in the refusal messages is deliberate. A model told "cannot switch" tries again; a model told "delegate this to a local subagent, or pick a larger-window route, here are the token counts" stops burning turns on it.

## Install

Installed from a git tag of this repository — it is not published to npm. Replace `<version>` with a released version (tags are named `dsh-model-switch-v<version>`; see [the tag list](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags)):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-switch-v<version>&path:/packages/model-switch"
```

That installs the package into the profile and enables its bundle. If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent is below — then also add `dsh-model-switch` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, because `pnpm add` alone installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-switch-v<version>&path:/packages/model-switch"
```

> **Warning:** never `pnpm add dsh-model-switch` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-model-switch`) by bare name. That resolves from the npm registry, where the package called `dsh-model-switch` belongs to an unrelated author and is **not** this plugin.

Restart dsh. With no configuration you get `switch_model`, the fit guard, the pill and the banner. `switch_model_escalate` is **not** offered until you designate the escalation route — see below.

## Configuration

Set these on the row in your own profile patch (`config:` block), or via your deployment's equivalent:

| Key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `escalationProvider` + `escalationModel` | *unset* | Where `switch_model_escalate` hands the session. **Unset means the tool is not registered at all** — a model that cannot see it will not reach for it, which beats a tool whose every call fails. |
| `readerProvider` + `readerModel` | *unset* | A route whose window can read the whole conversation. The one-click repair moves there, compacts, and returns. Without it the repair refuses and says exactly what to configure. |
| `preferredRoutes` | `[reader]` | Ordered `provider/model` recommendations when a conversation outgrows its route. Needed because "smallest window that still fits" often lands on a different provider that merely declares the same number. |
| `fitRatio` | `0.8` | Fraction of a destination window treated as usable. It is dsh-compaction-basic's own default compaction point, so the guard agrees with what the harness would do anyway. |
| `summaryReserveTokens` | `10000` | Room left for the summary checkpoint compaction writes. |
| `autoCompact` | `true` | When `false`, the guard never compacts on its own: a too-big switch is refused with the `/compact` instruction instead. |

Compaction retries are fixed internal limits, not configuration (`maxRegionAttempts` is 8 and `maxCompactionAttempts` is 3; setting either in the row is ignored with an unknown-key warning).

Resolution lives in [`src/config.mjs`](./src/config.mjs) and is [tested](./test/config.test.mjs). It is stricter than most plugins on purpose: a misspelled key, a YAML `"0.8"`, or an escalation provider with no model each print one warning at boot, because a misconfiguration you see once is worth much less debugging than one you discover at the first switch.

Example, on a deployment with a cloud big-window route and a local workhorse:

```yaml
- id: model-switch
  name: dsh-model-switch
  config:
    escalationProvider: cloud
    escalationModel: cloud-frontier
    readerProvider: cloud
    readerModel: cloud-long-context
    preferredRoutes:
      - cloud/cloud-long-context
      - cloud/cloud-frontier
```

## How the guard decides

`switch_model` measures the session (via dsh's replay-based token meter — no model call), resolves the destination window, and picks one of five outcomes in [`src/fit.mjs`](./src/fit.mjs):

| Situation | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| No measurement, or the destination declares no window | **allow** with a note. The guard never blocks a switch it cannot evaluate. |
| Fits under the margin | **allow** |
| Doesn't fit, and the current route cannot compact it (transcript over `fitRatio` of its window) | **refuse**, with token counts and the delegate-to-subagent alternative |
| Doesn't fit, `autoCompact: false` | **refuse**, with the `/compact` instruction |
| Doesn't fit but is compactable here | **compact first**, re-measure, then allow — reporting how much was freed |

One subtlety that cost a bug each way: the *fit* margin (0.8) decides whether to compact, while "can this route read the transcript" uses the **route's own window**. Using the margin for both meant a session at 85% of its own window was shipped off to another route and back for a compaction it could have done itself.

## Compatibility

Requires dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or later. Declared in `package.json` under `engines.dsh` and on every `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer as `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`. dsh checks these ranges itself, counting prereleases, so it accepts every harness build from 0.2.0-rc.2 on; on a harness outside them `dsh plugin add` refuses the install, and a profile that already has it skips the bundle with a log line. pnpm's own peer check is narrower: it admits only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases (plus every stable release from 0.2.0), so on other prereleases it reports a peer mismatch that dsh does not.

## Session format

The handoff message this plugin steers into a session after a switch carries
`source: { kind: 'plugin:model-switch', form: 'notice', summary }`. dsh 0.2.0
sessions (format V4) reject the shared `'plugin'` kind on read, so the producer name
lives in `kind`. Sessions written by dsh 0.1.x with the old kind are rewritten to
this same value by dsh's own migrator.

## Troubleshooting

**"switch_model_escalate" is not offered.** Expected until `escalationProvider`/`escalationModel` are set. The boot log says so.

**A switch was refused that should have worked.** Read the numbers in the refusal. If it says the current route cannot read the conversation, that is real: ask for a compact while still on a big-window route, or delegate to a subagent (which starts with a fresh, small context) instead.

**The pill/banner shows nothing.** It needs a *routed request* — a session that has not sent a message yet has no measurement. It also needs the plugin's client half to load: check the browser console for a `slot entry crashed` line naming this plugin.

**The repair button is missing.** Repair needs compaction reachable through `dsh-compaction-basic` (or the `/compact` command). A profile without compaction composed cannot offer it.

## Development

Plain ESM, no build step:

```sh
node --test packages/model-switch/test/*.test.mjs    # fit guard + config resolution
node scripts/verify.mjs --package dsh-model-switch   # release contract
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs model-switch          # real dsh composition
node scripts/check-plugin-hooks.mjs                  # React hook-order gate for the client half
```

`src/fit.mjs`, `src/config.mjs`, `src/notice.mjs` and `src/guard.mjs` (services injected) hold every decision worth testing and import nothing from dsh, which is what lets the suites run on a bare `git clone`. `src/host.mjs` is the Cordis wiring; `src/client.mjs` is the browser half. See [`../../docs/authoring.md`](../../docs/authoring.md).

## License

MIT

# dsh-plugins

Public [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins by [Chris Johnson](https://github.com/chrisjohnson). One repository, independently installable plugins — each with its own README, its own tests, its own changelog and its own version.

## Install

**Nothing here is published to npm.** Every release is a git tag on this repository, named `<package>-v<version>` (for example `dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1`), and you install a plugin by pinning that tag plus the package's subdirectory:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

`dsh plugin add` hands that spec to pnpm and also lists the package under the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, which is what activates its configuration layer. If you manage a profile's `package.json` yourself, the same spec works with pnpm directly — but then add the package name to `dsh.profile.bundles` by hand, because a plain `pnpm add` installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#<package>-v<version>&path:/packages/<dir>"
```

Pick the tag from [the repository's tags](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags); `<dir>` is the folder under `packages/` in the index below.

> **Warning — do not install these by bare name.** `pnpm add dsh-model-switch` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-model-switch`) resolves against the npm registry, and the npm package called `dsh-model-switch` belongs to an unrelated author: it is **not** this plugin. The same can happen to any unscoped `dsh-*` name. Always use the git-tag spec above.

## Index

| Plugin | What it is for | Latest | Directory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **[dsh-model-switch](./packages/model-switch/)** | Let the agent switch its own model mid-session, with a context-window fit guard so neither it nor a human in the composer can strand a conversation on a model too small to read it. | 0.2.1 | `packages/model-switch` |
| **[dsh-image-search-searxng](./packages/image-search-searxng/)** | A model-facing `image_search` tool over your own SearXNG, rendered inline in the Web GUI. | 0.2.0 | `packages/image-search-searxng` |
| **[dsh-continue-kicker](./packages/continue-kicker/)** | Automatically send "continue" when a turn halts on the output-token limit (or after a crash, or on a reasoning-only empty stop), with a runaway guard that stops after repeated kicks with no progress. | 0.2.0 | `packages/continue-kicker` |
| **[dsh-loop-watchdog](./packages/loop-watchdog/)** | Detect an agent stuck in a loop before each step (a deterministic repetition check plus an optional model judge), keep an audit ledger of every check, optionally steer the session, and chart the ledger in a `dsh-better-sidebar` panel. | 0.1.0 | `packages/loop-watchdog` |
| **[dsh-scheduled-queue](./packages/scheduled-queue/)** | Schedule the composer's draft to be sent to its own session later, with a per-session dock to edit, cancel or send now. Runs alongside the official schedule bundle. | 0.1.0 | `packages/scheduled-queue` |
| **[dsh-kanban](./packages/kanban/)** | Ticket-centric work organizer and code-driven workflow engine: a local SQLite board whose phases spawn sandboxed role sessions, gate on per-provider capacity, verify machine-readable conditions, and record a complete time/token ledger. | 0.1.0 | `packages/kanban` |
| **[dsh-model-capacity](./packages/model-capacity/)** | Process-wide, per-provider model-call capacity: every call — an interactive turn or a subagent child's — queues FIFO for its provider, and a panel inspects active leases and waiters. | 0.4.0 | `packages/model-capacity` |
| **[dsh-better-git-worktree](./packages/better-git-worktree/)** | Run a session in its own self-contained git working copy: a composer Worktree switch, a `worktree_convert` tool, session-list status badges, a header menu, and an archive prompt that decides the working copy's fate. | 0.1.1 | `packages/better-git-worktree` |
| **[dsh-session-cost](./packages/session-cost/)** | A compact estimated-cost badge in the composer stats bar: reads the session billed-token buckets and prices them with public models.dev rates, hidden at $0. | 0.1.0 | `packages/session-cost` |
| **[dsh-math-literal](./packages/math-literal/)** | Keeps single-`$` dollars literal in web chat: unpaired `$` in settled markdown renders as a literal dollar sign (matching the streaming arm) instead of opening an inline-math pair, while real math and code regions are untouched. | 0.1.0 | `packages/math-literal` |
| **[dsh-browser](./packages/browser/)** | One browser context per DSH session on a single shared remote Browserless connection for `dsh-playwright-browser`'s tools, with reconnect after a dropped connection, context cleanup when a session ends, and an announced local fallback. | 0.1.0 | `packages/browser` |

Install lines for the latest release of each package:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-switch-v0.2.1&path:/packages/model-switch"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-image-search-searxng-v0.2.0&path:/packages/image-search-searxng"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-continue-kicker-v0.2.0&path:/packages/continue-kicker"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-loop-watchdog-v0.1.0&path:/packages/loop-watchdog"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-scheduled-queue-v0.1.0&path:/packages/scheduled-queue"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-kanban-v0.1.0&path:/packages/kanban"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-model-capacity-v0.4.0&path:/packages/model-capacity"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-better-git-worktree-v0.1.1&path:/packages/better-git-worktree"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-session-cost-v0.1.0&path:/packages/session-cost"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-math-literal-v0.1.0&path:/packages/math-literal"
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-browser-v0.1.0&path:/packages/browser"
```

Each package's README is the contract: what it does, every configuration key and what happens when it is unset, how it fails, how to install it, and how to run its checks. Nothing important lives only here.

## Releases

1. A release is a normal pull request that bumps one package's version and moves its CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry under that version.
2. After it merges, the tag `<package>-v<version>` is cut on that merge commit and pushed. Nothing is committed directly to `main`.
3. Consumers pin the tag with the install spec above. A tag is never moved or rewritten once pushed.

Details: [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## What "a plugin from this repo" means

- **Plain ESM, no build step.** `git clone && npm test` works with nothing installed. No bundler, no TypeScript layer, no generated client — what the harness loads is what is in `src/`.
- **Every plugin declares `dsh.bundle.patch`**, so one command installs *and* activates it; nothing here needs a hand-edited `cordis.yml`.
- **Deployment-specific values are configuration, never defaults.** A plugin that "works on my machine" because it hard-codes my provider ids is broken for everyone else. `node scripts/verify.mjs` fails the build on author-local paths and provider ids.
- **Nothing is required to be configured.** Optional features report themselves unavailable and name the key that enables them, instead of throwing at boot or failing at first use.
- **Every decision worth testing lives in a module that imports nothing from dsh**, which is what makes the tests real rather than decorative.

## Checking this repository

```sh
npm run check          # verify + hook gate + all tests, no install needed
node scripts/verify.mjs            # the release contract (see below)
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs     # install into a throwaway profile, import, compose
```

`scripts/verify.mjs` is the interesting one: it enforces the rules that make a plugin installable and trustworthy — `dsh.bundle.patch` present and loading the package by name, `dsh.client` matched by an `./client` export, one harness peer range across every package (`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`; dsh checks it with prereleases included, while plain node-semver/pnpm admit only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases from it), every shipped file inside the `files` allowlist (all a git-tag install ships), a git-tag install line (and no bare-name one) in every package README, every config key documented in its README, every package listed in the index above, and no deployment leakage. It runs on CI for every push and it runs on a bare clone.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). If you are an agent working in this repository, read [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) first; it is short and it exists because these plugins run with your user's credentials.

For how these plugins get developed, tested against a live harness, released and consumed by the deployment they came from, see [docs/testing.md](./docs/testing.md) and [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

# dsh-scheduled-queue

**Schedule the message in your composer to be sent later, into the same session.**

A composer feature for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): type a message, press the clock button beside Send, choose how many minutes from now, and the message is delivered to that session when the time comes — even if the session has been stopped in the meantime, and even if the harness restarts first.

| What | Where | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clock button | composer, before the Send action | Enabled while the draft has text. Opens a small dialog: send in N minutes, optionally as **force steer**. |
| Scheduled-messages dock | above the composer card | Lists **this session's** scheduled messages with a live countdown. Each row can be edited (text, minutes, force steer — editing restarts the countdown), removed, or sent now. Hidden when the session has none. |
| Delivery | host | A scanner checks for due items; each is sent exactly like a normal composer send. |

A scheduled message is the user's own text. It arrives in the transcript as an ordinary user message (source kind `user`), not as a plugin notice.

## Per-session scope

Both composer slots are scoped to one session window and are handed that session's id. The dock shows, and the host returns, only the items scheduled for that session: a message scheduled in session A is not visible in, and cannot be edited, removed or sent from, session B. A call that does not name a session gets no items back rather than everything.

## Delivery

When an item is due the host calls `sessionController.prompt` with the item's id as the request id — the same call the composer's Send button makes.

- **Normal item** — a follow-up: it runs as its own turn after the current one.
- **Force steer item** — steering: it interrupts the current turn at the next step.
- **Session not running** — the session is resumed first, then the message is delivered.
- **Retries** — a delivery that fails stays queued and is retried with a back-off (5 s, doubling, capped at 5 min). A delivery that gets no answer within `deliveryTimeoutMs` is given up on and counts as a failure, so one hung session cannot hold up the others; the item is retried later. The harness only checks the abort signal before it admits a prompt, so a prompt that was already admitted may still land. The retry then carries the same request id, which `prompt` dedupes on, so it cannot send twice.
- **Session not found** — the harness also reports this transiently (a session disposed while the message was being admitted), so the host asks once more after two seconds. Only if the session is still not found is the item dropped, with a warning that includes the message text (first 500 characters).
- **Rejected by the harness** (`gateway/bad-request`, e.g. empty content) — retrying cannot help, so the item is dropped with a warning that includes its text.
- **Sorting** — due items are delivered oldest-due first.
- **Time zone** — the browser's time zone is stored with the item when it is scheduled and passed as `clientTimeZone`, so time-aware context sees a zone. Only `UTC` and `Area/Location` names are kept (the harness rejects anything else, such as `GMT`, `EST` or `+05:00`); otherwise the field is left off. If the harness still refuses a stored zone, the send is retried once without it. Items without one (queued by earlier versions) are sent without.
- **Disposal** — when the plugin is unloaded the scanner stops, in-flight calls are aborted, and nothing more is sent or written.

## How this differs from the official schedule bundle

dsh 0.2.0 ships an optional `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-schedule-bundle` (rows `time-context`, `schedule`, `ui-schedule`). Both can be enabled together. They solve different problems:

| | `dsh-scheduled-queue` (this) | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-schedule-bundle` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who schedules | **You**, from the composer | **The agent**, through tools (`schedule_create`, `schedule_list`, `schedule_update`, `schedule_delete`), and you, from the task page |
| What | One-shot "send this text in N minutes" | One-shot, fixed-rate, daily, weekly and cron reminders with titles and delivery history |
| Surface | Clock button and dock in the composer | Task page, session-row marks, header utilities |
| Storage | `<dsh home>/storages/scheduled-queue.json` | `schedule.json` in the harness's storage domain |

Why both exist: the official bundle is a task manager for recurring and agent-created reminders. This plugin is a "send this later" button on the draft you are looking at, with the pending messages visible beside the composer. Neither replaces the other.

Nothing collides, so no setup is needed to run them side by side. Checked against 0.2.0-rc.2:

- **Plugin rows:** this plugin is `scheduled-queue`; the bundle inserts `time-context`, `schedule`, `ui-schedule`.
- **Tools:** this plugin registers none; the bundle's are `schedule_create`, `schedule_list`, `schedule_update`, `schedule_delete`.
- **Slots:** this plugin uses `conversation.input.right` (id `sq-clock`) and `conversation.input.dock` (id `sq-dock`), both additive list slots. The bundle's client mounts into `conversation.session.header.utilities`, `conversation.chat.turnTail`, `sidebar.*` and `shell.overlay`, not these.
- **Routes:** this plugin owns `/api/scheduledQueue/*`; the bundle's service uses the typed `schedule` remote namespace.
- **Storage:** different files, different formats.
- **Client module id and styles:** `dsh-scheduled-queue`, style tag `sq-styles`, CSS classes `sq-*`.

One practical consequence: a message queued here is not visible to the agent's `schedule_list`, and a reminder created through the bundle does not show in this plugin's dock.

## Replacing the in-tree plugin

If your deployment still carries the earlier copy (dsh-deploy's `.dsh/profiles/web/plugins/scheduled-queue` and its `scheduled-queue` row in `cordis.patch.yml`), remove or keep disabled that row **before** enabling this package. Two plugins would register the same `/api/scheduledQueue/*` routes (the second registration fails) and scan the same queue file. The queue file is shared and compatible, so items already queued carry over.

## Install

Installed from a git tag of this repository — it is not published to npm. Replace `<version>` with a released version (tags are named `dsh-scheduled-queue-v<version>`; see [the tag list](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags)):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-scheduled-queue-v<version>&path:/packages/scheduled-queue"
```

That installs the package into the profile and enables its bundle. If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent is below — then also add `dsh-scheduled-queue` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, because `pnpm add` alone installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-scheduled-queue-v<version>&path:/packages/scheduled-queue"
```

> **Warning:** never `pnpm add dsh-scheduled-queue` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-scheduled-queue`) by bare name. That resolves from the npm registry, where an unscoped `dsh-*` name can belong to an unrelated author and is **not** this plugin.

Restart dsh. With no configuration you get the clock button, the dock and delivery.

## Configuration

Set these on the row in your own profile patch (`config:` block). A top-level config-only row replaces the whole `config` object, so list every key you want.

| Key | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scanIntervalMs` | `5000` | How often, in milliseconds, the host looks for due items. Clamped to 1000–60000; a value that is not a number is ignored with a warning naming the key. Unset = 5000. |
| `deliveryTimeoutMs` | `60000` | How long one delivery may take before it is given up on and retried. Clamped to 1000–600000; same handling of bad values. Unset = 60000. |

Unknown keys are ignored with one warning each. Nothing is required.

## Persistence

The queue is one JSON file, `<dsh home>/storages/scheduled-queue.json`, where the dsh home is `$DSH_HOME` (a leading `~` is expanded), else `~/.dsh`. It is an array of

```json
{ "id": "…", "messageId": "…", "sessionId": "…", "text": "…", "minutes": 5, "forceSteer": false, "dueAt": 1700000000000, "createdAt": 1699999700000 }
```

Items are written on every change (to a temporary file, then renamed into place) and read at startup, before any request or delivery is served. Items queued by earlier versions use this same format and location and are picked up as they are; `timeZone` is an optional field added later. A file that is not a JSON array is moved aside to `scheduled-queue.json.corrupt-<time>` and the queue starts empty, rather than being overwritten. A file that exists but cannot be read (permissions, I/O error) is logged loudly and **never written over**: the in-memory queue keeps working, nothing is persisted, and the read is retried on every scan; once it succeeds the restored items are merged in and the file is written.

## Host endpoints

Exact Fetch routes under the authenticated `/api` fence; the browser half calls them as `connection.rpc.call('/api', 'scheduledQueue/<endpoint>', payload)`.

| Endpoint | Payload | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schedule` | `sessionId`, `text`, `minutes`, `forceSteer` | `{ id, dueAt, queue }` for that session |
| `list` | `sessionId` (required) | `{ queue }` for that session |
| `remove` | `id`, `sessionId` | `{ removed, queue }` |
| `sendNow` | `id`, `sessionId` | `{ delivered, queue }` |
| `edit` | `id`, `sessionId`, any of `text`, `minutes`, `forceSteer` | `{ queue }`; empty text is refused |

Every endpoint requires `sessionId`; a call without one gets `bad-request`. `remove`, `edit` and `sendNow` answer `being-sent` for an item whose delivery is in flight.

## Known limits

- If the queue file exists but cannot be read, scheduling still works in memory and the dock warns that messages are not being saved yet. Nothing is written over the file; once it is readable again the restored items are merged in, without bringing back items that were delivered or removed in the meantime.

- **Archived sessions** accept the message and park it until the session is unarchived, exactly as a normal composer send does.
- **Overdue items** (due while the harness was down) wake and resume their sessions on the first scan after start-up. Several overdue items are delivered oldest-due first, one after another.
- **Send now** reports what happened: sent, "stays queued and is retried automatically", or "could not be delivered and was removed" (its text is in the host log). The notice appears even when the dock has no rows left.
- Scheduling does not clear the composer draft.
- The dock lists scheduled messages only for the session window it is in; there is no cross-session view.

## Checks

```sh
node --test packages/scheduled-queue/test/*.test.mjs
```

Covers the per-session filter (host and browser copies), scheduling and edit rules, back-off, the delivery request, reading earlier versions' queue files, and the host wiring against a stand-in harness. The browser rendering and a real delivery into a running session need a live harness and are checked by hand.

## Compatibility

dsh `>=0.2.0-rc.2`. Uses the `conversation.input.right` and `conversation.input.dock` slots, `connection.fetch.register`, and `sessionController.prompt`.

1. A release is a normal pull request that bumps one package's version and moves its CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry under that version.

## What "a plugin from this repo" means

- **Deployment-specific values are configuration, never defaults.** A plugin that "works on my machine" because it hard-codes my provider ids is broken for everyone else. `node scripts/verify.mjs` fails the build on author-local paths and provider ids.
- **Nothing is required to be configured.** Optional features report themselves unavailable and name the key that enables them, instead of throwing at boot or failing at first use.
- **Every decision worth testing lives in a module that imports nothing from dsh**, which is what makes the tests real rather than decorative.

## Checking this repository

```sh
npm run check          # verify + hook gate + all tests, no install needed
node scripts/verify.mjs            # the release contract (see below)
```

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). If you are an agent working in this repository, read [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) first; it is short and it exists because these plugins run with your user's credentials.

# dsh-session-cost

**A compact estimated-cost badge in the composer stats bar — the `$` you'd otherwise have to open a panel to find.**

One small pill, drawn next to the core token/cache stats (`14.6M tok · Cache hit 97%`) in the composer bar, showing the estimated cost of the session **and every descendant subagent** — the same "Agent Network" total the `dsh-context` Context tab shows. It reads each session's billed token buckets and prices them with public models.dev rates. It is a **button** with the core stats-pill hover, and **clicking it opens the session's Context tab**. It is **hidden while the total is $0**, so the composer row is unchanged on idle sessions and the number appears the moment the family burns tokens.

It is deliberately not a cost dashboard. `litellm` and the `dsh-context` Context Insights page already give full per-turn breakdowns; this is just the always-visible total.

## How it works

- **Data source.** The badge reads the `contextTimeline` session projection's `cost` field — the per-turn *billed* token buckets that `dsh-context` folds on every assistant settlement — for the session **and every descendant subagent**. It walks the parent→child session tree from the `useSessions` store (the same way `dsh-context` builds its Agent Network card) and sums each node's buckets:

  ```
  cost[provider][model][period] = { uncached, cacheRead, cacheWrite, output }
  period ∈ { "peak", "off" }
  ```

  Reading the same buckets `dsh-context` uses keeps the badge's token counts identical to the Context Insights page (no second token-counting pass).

- **Pricing.** Each bucket is priced with the models.dev per-million rate for that model, then summed. The rate source and formula mirror `dsh-context` exactly: the badge fetches `https://models.dev/api.json` (the same catalog `dsh-context` reads, once per page load) and resolves each model the same way — the mapped models.dev provider, then a `deepseek-` prefix, then the model-name index — so it covers every model the Context Insights page prices and shows the same number. The DeepSeek peak rule is preserved: for a DeepSeek provider the **peak** period (Beijing-time workday windows) bills at 2× the off-peak/list rate. The pure resolution + fold live in `src/prices.mjs`; the browser half fetches the catalog and carries a tiny inline `deepseek-flash` catalog as the offline fallback.

- **Where.** The entry is registered into the `conversation.composer.dock` slot (the same slot the core stats pill owns), placed after the token/cache pill. It renders a single `$`-formatted **button** styled like the core StatsPills (same tertiary label color, inherited font, tabular numerals) **with the core's interactive hover** (interactive background + secondary label) and pointer cursor. **Clicking it switches the session to the Context tab** — there is no plugin-facing view-switch API, so it clicks the tab bar's Context tab the way a user would (and degrades to a no-op if that tab isn't found, e.g. a non-English label). Nothing else — no panel, no dialog, no settings.

## Install

Installed from a git tag of this repository — it is not published to npm. Replace `<version>` with a released version (tags are named `dsh-session-cost-v<version>`; see [the tag list](https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins/tags)):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-session-cost-v<version>&path:/packages/session-cost"
```

If you manage the profile's `package.json` yourself, the pnpm equivalent is below — then also add `dsh-session-cost` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, because `pnpm add` alone installs the plugin without enabling it:

```sh
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/chrisjohnson/dsh-plugins.git#dsh-session-cost-v<version>&path:/packages/session-cost"
```

> **Warning:** never `pnpm add dsh-session-cost` (or `dsh plugin add dsh-session-cost`) by bare name. That resolves from the npm registry, where an unscoped `dsh-*` name may belong to an unrelated author and is **not** this plugin.

Restart dsh. With no configuration the badge is live.

## Configuration

There is none. The badge has no user-facing settings — it prices whatever models the session already used, from a public rate table. The bundle patch row carries an empty `config` on purpose.

## Notes and limits

- **It is an estimate.** Token counts are the provider-reported billed totals; only the dollars-per-token conversion is an estimate, from public models.dev list rates. It will not match a billing invoice to the cent, and it is not a spend-control.
- **DeepSeek peak pricing only applies when the provider is recognised as DeepSeek.** The peak×2 rule fires for the dsh provider ids `deepseek-official` and `deepseek-account` (the ones `dsh-context` maps to models.dev `deepseek`). A session routed through a deployment-owned proxy (for example a local LiteLLM gateway that forwards to DeepSeek) is **not** in that map, so it is priced at flat list rates with no peak/off split — the same thing `dsh-context` does for such a provider, so the two surfaces stay consistent. To apply the peak rule to a proxy, add its dsh provider id to `MODELS_DEV_PROVIDER_IDS` in `src/prices.mjs`.
- **Unknown models are hidden.** If a session used a model the live models.dev catalog has no per-million rate for (no `input`/`output`), the badge shows nothing rather than a guess — the same model coverage `dsh-context` has, because both read the same catalog.
- **It makes one network fetch.** The browser fetches `https://models.dev/api.json` once per page load to build the rate book (the same request `dsh-context` makes); the badge stays hidden until it lands. If the fetch fails (offline), a tiny inline `deepseek-flash` catalog is used, so the common DeepSeek case still prices.
- **Depends on `dsh-context` for the buckets.** The badge reads the `contextTimeline` projection that `dsh-context` maintains. If `dsh-context` is not enabled in the profile, the badge has no data and stays hidden. It does not otherwise touch or configure `dsh-context`.
- **Subagents are summed (Agent Network total).** The badge shows the cost of the session it is drawn for **plus every descendant subagent session** — the same "Agent Network" figure the `dsh-context` Context tab shows (current agent + subagents, all levels). Each subagent's `contextTimeline.cost` is read via the parent→child session tree and summed; because pricing is linear in the buckets, the per-session sums equal the family total. On a subagent-less session this is just that session's own cost, so single-session numbers are unchanged from 0.2.0.

## Checks

- `node --test packages/session-cost/test/*.test.mjs` — unit tests for the price-book build, model resolution (provider map, `deepseek-` prefix, index fallback), the cost fold, the peak/off rule, and the formatting.
- `node scripts/check-plugin-hooks.mjs` — the browser half is a single hook call over a stable fallback, so the Rules-of-Hooks gate passes.
- `node scripts/verify.mjs` — the release contract (install line, files allowlist, peer range, no deployment leakage).

1. A release is a normal pull request that bumps one package's version and moves its CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry under that version.
2. After it merges, the tag `<package>-v<version>` is cut on that merge commit and pushed. Nothing is committed directly to `main`.
3. Consumers pin the tag with the install spec above. A tag is never moved or rewritten once pushed.

Details: [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## What "a plugin from this repo" means

- **Plain ESM, no build step.** `git clone && npm test` works with nothing installed. No bundler, no TypeScript layer, no generated client — what the harness loads is what is in `src/`.
- **Every plugin declares `dsh.bundle.patch`**, so one command installs *and* activates it; nothing here needs a hand-edited `cordis.yml`.
- **Deployment-specific values are configuration, never defaults.** A plugin that "works on my machine" because it hard-codes my provider ids is broken for everyone else. `node scripts/verify.mjs` fails the build on author-local paths and provider ids.
- **Nothing is required to be configured.** Optional features report themselves unavailable and name the key that enables them, instead of throwing at boot or failing at first use.
- **Every decision worth testing lives in a module that imports nothing from dsh**, which is what makes the tests real rather than decorative.

## Checking this repository

```sh
npm run check          # verify + hook gate + all tests, no install needed
node scripts/verify.mjs            # the release contract (see below)
node scripts/compose-smoke.mjs     # install into a throwaway profile, import, compose
```

`scripts/verify.mjs` is the interesting one: it enforces the rules that make a plugin installable and trustworthy — `dsh.bundle.patch` present and loading the package by name, `dsh.client` matched by an `./client` export, one harness peer range across every package (`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.3.0-0`; dsh checks it with prereleases included, while plain node-semver/pnpm admit only `0.2.0-rc.*` and `0.3.0-*` prereleases from it), every shipped file inside the `files` allowlist (all a git-tag install ships), a git-tag install line (and no bare-name one) in every package README, every config key documented in its README, every package listed in the index above, and no deployment leakage. It runs on CI for every push and it runs on a bare clone.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). If you are an agent working in this repository, read [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) first; it is short and it exists because these plugins run with your user's credentials.

For how these plugins get developed, tested against a live harness, released and consumed by the deployment they came from, see [docs/testing.md](./docs/testing.md) and [docs/releasing.md](./docs/releasing.md).

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
dsh-connect-qoder

把 Qoder（通义灵码国内版 / 国际版）的模型接入 DeepSeek Harness，并提供账号池、每日签到、积分读数与模型管理。

English · 安装 · 工作原理 · 配置 · 账号池 · 更新日志 · 问题反馈

一个独立的 [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) bundle 插件。它把 Qoder 账号的模型接到 DSH 的模型选择器，同时提供模型管理与只读的用量概览。**国内版与国际版是两个并行的供应商（`qoder` / `qoder-global`），可同时使用**；插件设置卡片以 tab 区分两者，方便统一管理。 > Qoder 官方不提供 OpenAI 兼容端点（其官方 SDK 只是 agent 启动器），因此本插件直连 Qoder 的 cosy 网关，实现了协议的最小客户端，无需在 Qoder 桌面端登录——只需一个 PAT（Personal Access Token）。 ## 功能特性 - **双供应商并行接入（国内版 + 国际版）** —— 国内版注册为 `qoder` provider（`gateway.qoder.com.cn`），国际版注册为 `qoder-global` provider（`api1.qoder.sh`）。**配置了 PAT 的区域其模型会出现在 DSH 模型选择器里**：两个区域都有 PAT 时两组同时可选，不同会话可以各选一边，互不干扰。**没有 PAT 的区域不列出任何模型**（一个请求也发不出去，列出来只会点到就失败）；配置 PAT 后「刷新模型」即可让模型自动出现——provider 本身始终注册着，因为它的设置卡片正是配置入口。模型名内嵌上游积分倍率（如 `Qwen3.8-Flash · x0.00`），与 Qoder 自身模型菜单一致。 - **插件卡片 tab 切换** —— 设置卡片顶部为「国内版 / 国际版」两个 tab，各含独立的 PAT、模型管理与用量概览；每个 tab 的目录、勾选与状态完全隔离。 - **正文按「账号 / 模型 / 诊断」分栏** —— 每个区域 tab 之下再把正文分成三栏。账号栏是账号池、积分读数开关与关于凭据的每一条说明（点一下即生效）；模型栏是勾选、上下文档位、思考强度与逐模型测试（草稿，点「保存」才落地）——两者的提交语义本来就不同，分开之后保存按钮就挨着它保存的东西。**切栏不重新拉取、不丢未保存的草稿**（非活动栏仍挂载）。诊断栏是一张只读的事实表：区域、**上游域名**（与真正发请求的主机名同一处事实）、服务账号、凭据来源、积分读取时刻、目录模型数、已启用数、账号池开关，以及上游最近一次错误的**原文**——它存在的唯一理由是被整段贴进问题反馈，所以里面没有任何会改设置的控件。 - **可单独关闭任一版本供应商** —— 每个 tab 右侧有一个勾选框（默认都勾选）。**取消勾选即把该供应商从 DSH 模型选择器里彻底撤掉**（不是只藏起 tab）：它的路由与「设置 → 模型」页的目录条目一并摘除。PAT、用量与勾选**全部保留**，重新勾选即完整恢复。注意：若某会话此前选中的正是被关闭供应商的模型，该会话再调用会报 `NO_ADAPTER`。 - **模型管理** —— 从上游刷新完整模型目录，逐项勾选启用或禁用；模型行显示倍率（`(0.50x)`）、上下文/输出上限、思考强度档位与免费标记，行右有「图片」「可关闭思考」开关、上下文档位选择器与「测试」按钮。勾选状态写入本地配置，立即同步到模型选择器。**目录里有几个模型就排几行，列表自己不设高度上限、不出内滚动条**——这条列表的用途是「看见并勾选模型」，只露七八行、把其余的藏进第二条滚动条（面板本身已经在滚）会让「有这个模型吗」变成一个需要先发现、再去拖的动作；要看全就滚页面。**上游的 `auto` 不列出来**：它是该区的默认**路由**，网关在请求时才决定把它解析成哪个模型，所以价格与上下文都由别人临时决定，插件无法如实描述——它不是模型，不该占一行让你勾选。 - **活动优惠徽标** —— 上游在模型目录里自带活动规则（`promotion`：文案、时段、时区），模型行就在名字旁画一枚小胶囊，如「错峰 4 折」。**文案原样来自上游**（中文界面取 `badge.zh`，英文界面取 `badge.en`），插件不翻译也不改写；悬停给出上游的说明、时段与时区，以及活动文档链接原文。什么时候画由**渲染时刻**决定：有上游声明的墙钟时段（支持跨零点、按上游时区算）就按时段现算，没有时段才退回上游的 `active`——所以夜里读到的目录不会把徽标冻结到第二天早上，早上启动的进程也不会因此整晚不显示；没有活动字段的模型什么都不画。同一枚徽标也画在宿主的**模型选择器**里（`conversation.input.model.label` 槽位，issue #12）——选择器才是做选择的地方，与卡片共用同一套判定、文案与样式。取证与判定规则见 [docs/PROMO_BADGE.md](docs/PROMO_BADGE.md)。 - **模型可用性测试** —— 每个模型行有一个「测试」按钮，直达上游确认该模型此刻能否使用：限流（429）报「被限流」、凭据无效报「凭据无效」、内容审核拒绝报「内容被审核拒绝」、额度耗尽报「额度已耗尽」，其余上游瞬时故障如实分类。探测在后台发起，**凭据不会传到页面**；结果不写入设置，也不改变你已保存的勾选。**它发的是真实请求**（会消耗少量上游额度），因此只能按单个模型手工点，没有「测试已勾选」这类批量按钮。 - **每日签到** —— Qoder 有官方每日签到活动（个人用户每天可领 100 Credits，30 天有效）。账号池提供「一键签到所有账号」：逐账号领取、已领过的按幂等处理（不重复领取、不算失败），签到后积分自动刷新。国内版与国际版都已接通（国际版需要本机 Qoder 客户端的设备风控组件，取不到时如实报错而不是假装「今天没有活动」）。 - **活动（只读）** —— 卡片在区域作用域内、额度读数之下多一条「活动」列表，逐条列出上游当前下发的活动：每日 100 Credits 签到行（带额度与「可领取 / 已领取」状态）与「1024 创造力集结」「首月订阅 Credits 翻倍」这类 banner（`VIEW_DETAILS`）。**标题与描述原样来自上游**（按界面语言取 `zh` / `en`，缺哪边用另一边），「查看详情」是真正的链接（上游的 `detailUrl`，缺失时退回活动落地页）；**只读**，不签到、不改账号。上游没下发就显示「当前没有活动」，读不到则显示原因（不是装作没有）。此前本插件只读签到用的那一小片活动数据，banner 行被整行跳过（用户实拍 2026-10-25），现已整份读取。 - **积分（只读）** —— 账号池逐账号显示剩余积分与最近积分包的到期时间（来自 Qoder 的 `sash/api/v2/me/usage`，凭 `jt-` jobToken 查询）；临期的积分包会高亮。查询是**只读**的、不消耗积分；读不到时（凭据被拒 / 上游未响应）如实说明原因并给出路，不留一片空白。 - **安全 loopback shim** —— 每区域一个随机端口 + 进程内随机 secret，真实 Qoder PAT **不交给 pi-ai**：pi-ai 只与本地 shim 对话，shim 用 cosy 会话（jobToken）做上游请求。 - **多账号池（PAT）** —— 每区域一个本地 vault `$DSH_HOME/.qoder-accounts..json`（0600），把设置 PAT、环境变量与 vault 账号三源去重合并；卡片可新增（粘贴 `pt-…`，经 `JobToken` 交换校验并取显示名，也可自填备注名）/ 改名账号，也可显式选择某一账号服务（`regions..accountId`，留空自动按 settings → env → vault 选取）。**移出池**与**删除**是两件事：移出池 = 在池表格里取消勾选并保存（凭据留着，随时勾回）；删除 = 池表格行内的「删除」按钮，二次确认后抹掉 vault 里的 PAT 并自动退出池与区域选择（不可恢复；设置/环境变量里的 PAT 不归本插件管，不提供删除按钮）。 - **按实测排序与自动换号** —— 「一键测试所有账号」对池内每个成员发真实请求（目标模型默认自动挑本区域倍率为 0 的免费模型），结果落 `$DSH_HOME/.qoder-pool..json`；开启账号池后，聊天流在首字节前按 `rankPool`（可用性 → 快过期的积分优先 → 到期最近 → 积分高 → id）选出服务账号，失败时依次换下一个可用账号重试，失败回写 `live-request` 探测。关掉开关则插件不替你选、也不替你换，失败如实报错。**上游报额度耗尽必显示**：对话路径上一旦上游的业务码命中配额族（110 当日用量 / 113 配额 / 118 Credits 耗尽等），该区域卡片就出现一条「上游报额度耗尽」通知（最近一次时刻 + 业务码，悬停是脱敏后的上游原文）——与账号池开关无关，因为逐账号的 `out-of-credit` 明细只活在池视图里，池关着时这条通知是那次失败**唯一**可见的出口（0.7.x 的「今日额度疑似已用尽」胶囊拆掉后留下的缺口）。限流（HTTP 429 短窗）**不会**被标成耗尽——那是冷却，不是没额度。 - **账号转移（导入 / 导出）** —— 按区域把 vault 账号导出为传输文件，预览后按索引导入；跨区域域名（`qoder.com.cn` / `qoder.sh`）正向匹配，不匹配的记录计入 `skipped`。 - **思考强度与上下文预算** —— 上游按模型声明 `thinking_config.efforts`，卡片只列出**真实存在**的档位（Qwen 系 `low/medium/xhigh`、DeepSeek/GLM 系 `low/high/max`），选定即保存、每个请求自动带上（与 Qoder 客户端同一发送字段，双写顶层与 `parameters`）；上下文档位同样只来自上游 `context_config` 声明的档位，未声明时不渲染控件、不编造选项。 - **诚实的模型能力** —— 上游的 `is_vl` 是**平台**的图片输入声明而非模型原生能力，且它对几乎每个模型都是 `true`，所以本插件**不拿它当能力答案**，只认一张按精确 model id 键控的核对表：核对过的才预勾选，没核实的（含全新模型）一律不勾，并在开关 tooltip 里说明「为什么没勾」。表的依据是**厂商文档 + 真机实测**：2026-10-29 用「发一张画着数字 `7` 的图、问是哪个数字」逐个测了**两个区域目录并集里的全部 14 个模型**，**全部读图成功**，因此当前目录里没有纯文本模型（此前按命名推断的「code 系模型应是纯文本」被实测推翻）。「关闭思考」同样只对上游显式声明、且不在已知拒绝集里的模型提供。宁可少给一个选项，也不要让用户按下去就失败。 - **缓存命中如实上报** —— 上游的 `usage` 带 `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`，插件把它一路透传到宿主，所以 GUI 轮次统计里的「缓存命中」是真实比例（修复前这里恒显 0%：字段在归一路径上被丢掉了，那个 0% 是不可信的读数，不是缓存没生效的证据）。**命中数是 `prompt_tokens` 的子集，不是额外增量**——所以它不会被加进总数（那会把命中的前缀算两遍）。上游没报这个字段时就不写，不会用 0 顶替「不知道」。 - **composer 积分读数（位置可选）** —— 会话输入区按区域显示 `QD CN` / `QD AI` 与**当前计费账号**的余额（如 `QD CN · 92`；池接管时是接管者的余额，悬停写明归属），点开是逐账号的余额表，点某一行即切换到该账号，页头的「设置」按钮直接打开本插件的设置页；受每区域「在对话框显示积分」开关控制（默认开，opt-out）。**读数可放在两个位置之一**（卡片上的二选一下拉，每区域独立，默认不变）：**输入框工具栏**（`conversation.input.right`，紧挨模型选择器左侧、与权限切换器隔开）或**输入框下方**（`conversation.composer.dock`，即 shell 渲染轮次 / tok/s / token / 缓存命中那一行的常驻栏，读数是追加在自带统计之后）。之所以可选：输入框工具栏是**共享的 list 插槽**，另一个把东西停在那里的插件可能把读数挤到看不见——此时切到「输入框下方」即可（对齐 workbuddy issue #62）。 - **命令行诊断与现场验证** —— `dsh-connect-qoder doctor|status|logout [--json] [--region cn|global]`：`doctor` 报 PAT 来源、cosy 指纹派生、pi-ai 代际、宿主心跳存活与 vault 账号计数；`status` 报凭据来源、上游可达性与当前剩余积分；`logout` 清除指定区域的 vault 账号与账号池测量副本。另有 `pnpm run probe:cosy`（不依赖宿主直连 cosy 链路验证）与 `pnpm run probe:vault`（只读 dump vault / 账号池测量，PAT 只显示掩码）。 ## 工作原理 ```text DSH PiAiAdapter（每个 provider 一套） -> 安全 loopback shim（每区域一个随机端口 + 进程内随机 secret） -> QoderUpstreamClient（cosy 协议最小客户端） -> 国内版 https://gateway.qoder.com.cn/algo/api/v2/... -> 国际版 https://api1.qoder.sh/algo/api/v2/... -> Qoder SSE（OpenAI 形状增量） -> DSH 本地执行工具并回传结果 ``` 国内版与国际版各持一套完整的运行时栈——上游客户端、模型 catalog、回环 shim、adapter——按区域配置（网关 / openapi / 目录路径）隔离，所以**两个区域的模型可以同时可选、被不同会话使用**。 凭据是 PAT（设置卡片 `regions..pat` 或环境变量，见[配置](#配置)），设置项优先。每次会话按需惰性交换 **jobToken**：PAT 只在这个交换请求里使用一次，之后的对外请求全部携带 cosy bearer（自定义 Base64 载荷 + MD5 签名）与「机器指纹」会话头。**PAT 从不进入 pi-ai，也从不外发到网关之外；本插件不读不写 Qoder 桌面端的本地登录文件。** 模型的 cosy 编码与签名细节（自定义字母表、`n/3` 重排、`cosy&&` 签名、RSA/AES 会话封装）见 `src/cosy.ts` 的头部注释；错误分类（内容审核 / 限流 / 额度耗尽 / 瞬时故障）与 DSH 重试语义的对应见 `src/upstream.ts`。 ## 安装 ### 从发布包安装（推荐） ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop add @dmh2002/dsh-connect-qoder # Desktop dsh plugin 一台机器上往往有多个 Qoder 账号（多个 PAT）。**账号池**把这些账号收成一次点击：勾进池子，然后「一键签到所有账号」或「一键测试所有账号」；再打开**启用账号池**，插件就会在请求失败时自动换号接着跑。 **每个区域（国内版 / 国际版）各有独立的一池**：成员、目标模型、积分与签到状态互不影响——两边的账号本来就属于不同的供应商。**两个区域都有每日签到**：国际版的签到活动只下发给带设备风控头的请求，插件按区域读取本机 Qoder 客户端自带的设备身份组件；取不到时如实报错，不会把「拿不到设备身份」伪装成「今天没有活动」。 ### 自动换号（开启账号池即生效） - **谁来服务由排序决定**：开启后**每一次请求**都发给池内排序最靠前的可用账号，所以「当前使用」显示的是排序的结果，不一定是你手动选的那个。 - **失败时继续往下试**：某个请求在上游失败时，插件**依次**用池内其他可用账号重试，直到有一个接手、或全部不可用为止才把错误报出来。 - **哪些失败会换号**：429 限流、额度耗尽、401/403 凭据被拒、5xx 网关与网络故障——这些都是**某个账号**的状态，换一个很可能就过了。 - **哪些不会**：请求本身不合法（HTTP 400）——同一个请求体换谁都是同样的 400，重试只是让你多等几轮；**流已开始之后**也不会重放（字节已经发出去了）。 - **已知不可用的账号会被跳过**：处于限流冷却期内、或凭据已被上游拒绝的成员不参与选择。**从没测过的账号按「默认可用」参与**——刚添加的账号不该因为「还没测」就被排除。 - **手动选择从不被改写**：池子通过运行时覆盖决定「谁服务」，**不写回你保存的选择**；关掉开关，你选定的账号立刻完全生效。 - **失败会被记下来**：一次失败会写成该账号的测量（含上游报文中给出的恢复时间），下一个请求直接从可用账号开始，不必每次先撞一遍同一个限流账号。 - **换号会告诉你**：换号是插件替你做的决定，所以它会说出来——回答开头带一条引用块提示，例如 `> [dsh-connect-qoder] 「450702134816」被限流，已改用池中另一个账号回答。`。提示说的是**失败的那个账号**（你选中的那个），不点名接管者；连换多次只写一条，说的是紧邻换号的那次失败。没换号就一个字都不写。 ### 这个开关到底控制什么 **它只控制「插件要不要自己决定」，不控制「你能不能操作」。** | | 账号池 **开启** | 账号池 **关闭** | | --- | --- | --- | | 谁服务 | 由排序**自动**选出（可用优先 → 积分包快过期 → 到期最近 → 积分高 → id） | **你**在设置区的「使用哪个账号」里选定 | | 请求失败 | **自动**换下一个可用账号重试 | 不换号，如实报错 | | 一键签到 / 一键测试 | 可用 | **仍然可用** | | 目标测试模型 | 可改 | **仍然可改** | 最后两行是刻意的：签到与测试是**手动动作**，作用于你勾选的成员，与「插件是否自动路由」是两件事。 **唯一的硬约束**：池里一个成员都没勾选时，批量动作一律拒绝。空的池**绝不**退化成「那就对全部账号执行」——那是唯一会花掉你没授权过的积分的解读。 ### 重试预算可以调（`regions..retry`） 宿主有一个「原地重试」环：一次请求失败但值得再试时，它等一小段时间再发一次。等待阶梯由插件声明、宿主执行，默认跟随宿主（不填就是宿主的默认值，升级不会改变你现在的行为）。 Qoder 上游偶尔会回 `RESOURCE_LIMIT`（业务码 `10605`）并**自己申报**「请等 N 秒再来」。插件现在会把这个值写进给宿主的失败文案（形如 `[upstream retry-after 5s]`），你能直接看出上游只要求等多久，而不是只看到「上游报了个 4xx」。 想改预算就配这三个数字（都在区域级，两个区域各配各的）： ```yaml regions: cn: retry: maxRetries: 4 # 最多重试几次（0 = 跟随宿主默认） initialDelayMs: 5000 # 首次退避毫秒（0 = 跟随宿主默认） maxDelayMs: 30000 # 退避上限毫秒（0 = 跟随宿主默认） ``` 上面的 `5000 → 30000` 兼顾了上游两种常见形态：瞬时限流（申报 5 秒）与 `queueType:p2` 排队（约 30 秒）。**三个 0 表示跟随宿主默认**，所以留空与不写这个配置等价。 > 此前这一项只能是宿主的默认值，想调就得改 `node_modules` 里的构建产物 —— 而那会在升级时静默还原。 ### 排序规则（开启账号池后决定谁服务） 1. **可用优先** —— 被测量判定为不可用（限流未到恢复时间、凭据被拒等）的排到最后； 2. **积分高者优先** —— 只在有**新鲜读数**时参与（卡片轮询、批量测试或保存时读到的那份，10 分钟内有效）：请求路径**不会**为了排序去打上游，否则一页对话就变成 N 个额外请求； 3. **快过期的积分包优先** —— 3 天内到期的先花，过期即作废； 4. 最后按账号 id 收尾，保证顺序是**全序**、可复现。 ### 两个批量动作 - **一键签到所有账号** —— 逐个账号领取当日的官方签到活动。**先查状态再领取**，已领过的直接标「已签到」而**不发写入请求**（幂等，不重复领取）；任何单个账号失败只标记该行，**不中断整批**。签到会改变余额，因此批次结束后作废该区域的积分缓存，卡片不会继续显示领取前的数字。 - **一键测试所有账号** —— 对每个成员发一次真实请求，得出「这个账号此刻能不能用这个模型」。目标模型默认由「自动」挑本区域**倍率为 0 的免费模型**（多个候选取上下文窗口最大的），你也可以显式指定——但**在免费模型出现之前测试保持关闭**，避免在你不知情的情况下花掉积分。测试走的是与模型行同一套探测，因此**有真实成本**。 两种批量动作都**不锁住界面**：按钮自己变成「签到中… / 测试中…」，每处理完一个账号，那一行立刻落位、活动日志也**逐条**写下（时间戳是各自完成的那一刻，不是整批结束的那一秒）；其余界面照常可用。只有**保存配置**与**删除账号**会挡一道——前者在写盘、后者不可逆。 设置卡片的排布：顶部是**两格独立的供应商卡片**（国内版 / 国际版），每格自带边框与底色、右端有自己的开关，选中的那格描品牌色边——**一格就是一个单位**，点名字切 tab、点开关启用该供应商。再往下是「在对话框显示积分」与「显示位置」两行（整行可点，主标题下一行是说明），第三行是**可选的「在侧边栏显示 Qoder」**，然后是账号池、模型管理。这三行都是**立即生效，不需要点保存**：前两行管积分读数显不显示、显示在哪里，第三行管侧边栏那一行（以及它打开的整页）在不在。 不提供**自动**签到：签到会真实领取奖励，只在你点按钮时执行。 ## 命令行诊断 在**已装本插件的 profile 目录里**跑（推荐，无需全局安装）： ```bash cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop pnpm exec dsh-connect-qoder doctor # PAT 来源 + cosy 指纹派生 + pi-ai 代际 + 心跳 + vault 计数（纯本地，不发请求） pnpm exec dsh-connect-qoder status
