evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-pilot ## 让 DSH 看见并高效地操作你的电脑 **Give DeepSeek Harness hands and eyes on your desktop.** [![awesome · DSH plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg)](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/p/momasiku/dsh-pilot/) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@momasiku%2Fdsh-pilot?label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@momasiku/dsh-pilot) [![compat](https://github.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot/actions/workflows/compat.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot/actions/workflows/compat.yml) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) ![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows-0078d4.svg) [中文说明](#中文说明) · [English](#english) # 中文说明 > **给 DeepSeek Harness 装上眼睛和手——装在整个桌面上。** > > **范围**：Windows 桌面操控——模型看到的是真实屏幕，驱动的是真实鼠标与键盘。 DSH 原本只会"说"：它能推理、能写代码、能规划，但**看不见你的屏幕，也动不了你的鼠标**。于是看屏幕的是你、截图的是你、点按钮的是你、出错了汇报的也是你——你成了它的手、它的眼，还兼任它的报错信息。 **dsh-pilot 把这个环闭上**：模型直接看真实像素，然后自己动手。 ### 实例演示 ![dsh-pilot 在 AutoCAD 里画一块机械板：模型把 REC、角点坐标、内轮廓、五个圆、中心线和两道线性标注依次输入命令行，最后缩放到范围](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot/main/assets/dsh-pilot-cad.gif) **模型自己画出来的 CAD 图。** 用的就是 AutoCAD 自己的命令行——`REC` → `0,0` → `240,150`、内轮廓、五个圆孔、中心线、两道尺寸，**AutoCAD 里什么都没装**。 ![dsh-pilot 在 LibreOffice Calc 里改一列表头：聚焦工作簿、鼠标移到 C1、点击、粘贴「Q3 收入」、回车、Ctrl+S —— 全部在一次 desktop_sequence 调用里完成](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot/main/assets/dsh-pilot-excel.gif) **一次调用改完一张表。** `desktop_sequence` 聚焦工作簿、把鼠标移到 C1、点击、粘贴「Q3 收入」、回车、保存——整串动作只花一次往返。 ![dsh-pilot 在 Blender 里建模：先清空视口，加一个立方体，再用细分曲面把它磨成一个球，最后轨道旋转检查](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot/main/assets/dsh-pilot-blender.gif) **从零建一个 3D 模型。** 清空视口 → 加一个立方体 → `Ctrl+1`、`Ctrl+3` 两级细分，方盒子被磨成一个球。真机上的 Blender 4.2，跑在**一台没有显卡的机器**上——靠 Mesa 的软件 OpenGL，而那套环境也是模型自己配好的。 | 工具 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | **`screen_view`** | 抓取当前屏幕，把 PNG 作为**真正的图像块**交给模型（不是 OCR、不是文字描述），连光标位置、前台窗口、各显示器范围一起给出 | | **`desktop_control`** | 移动鼠标、单击/双击/右键、拖拽、滚轮、打字、按键、聚焦与列出窗口；可以在同一次调用里顺手截一张，让效果立刻可见 | | **`desktop_sequence`** | **一次调用跑完一整串动作**，最后只看一眼结果 | ## 它到底解决了什么 桌面自动化的瓶颈**从来不是鼠标点得快不快**，而是 **"模型和电脑要来回说多少次话"**： | 一个五步任务（聚焦窗口 → 点输入框 → 打字 → 回车 → 看结果） | 只用 DSH | DSH + dsh-pilot | | --- | --- | --- | | 谁在看屏幕 | 你 | 模型，看真实像素 | | 谁在点击打字 | 你 | 模型 | | 模型 ↔ 电脑往返次数 | 5 次（每步一次，外加你的） | **1 次** | | 送给模型的截图 | 4–5 张 | **1 张** | | 出错时 | 你发现、你描述 | 同一次结果里就写明哪一步、为什么 | ## 为什么坐标可信（这是"点得准"的关键） 视觉驱动点击最经典的翻车方式是"坐标差一点点"，这里堵掉了三个来源： 1. **两端都是 per-monitor DPI 感知**。非 DPI 感知的进程会被 Windows 骗——它把 2560×1600 的屏幕看成 1707×1067，于是按这种截图算出来的点击**必然偏**。传感器和执行器在做任何事之前都声明 `PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2`，所以一个图像像素就是一个物理屏幕像素。 2. **每张图都带坐标刻度尺**：上沿与左沿每 200px 一条刻度，标注的是**屏幕坐标**（不是图像偏移），还有 `origin x,y step n` 说明。模型直接读刻度，不用数像素；刻度是屏幕坐标，所以即使图片被压缩也依然有效。 3. **信封如实说明交付尺寸**。如果宿主把图压小了，模型会收到比例与乘数；坐标契约也变成条件式——**只有在"交付尺寸 == 采集尺寸"时**才承诺"照用 x、y 即可"，否则明确要求乘多少： ```text delivered 1974x873 = 0.873x capture; multiply image readings by 1.1454 to get screen pixels ``` ## 为什么快 批处理是大头（省的是往返，不是点击）；第二个大头是**不再每次重启 PowerShell**——一个常驻 worker 同时服务动作与截图： | 请求 | 一次性脚本 | 常驻 worker | | --- | --- | --- | | 动作（移动/点击/打字…） | ~0.9–2.0 秒 | **6–12 毫秒** | | 截图（主屏） | ~1.2–2.3 秒 | **~0.5 秒** | （2560×1600、150% 缩放、DSH 界面还在动的情况下实测）。worker 在第一次调用时后台预热，它需要的约 1 秒与第一张截图重叠，不会拖慢第一个动作。 **没变化的帧不重复发送**：每次截图都带 `frameHash`，与同会话上一帧逐字节相同时就不重复附图（也不重复存储），结果里写 `unchanged: true`，模型手上那张图的坐标继续有效；想看就传 `forceImage: true`。 ## 读控件树 截图是要靠猜的：模型在像素里找到按钮、估个中心、点一下，再截一张图看猜没猜对。 而 Windows 通过 UI Automation 直接把同一个控件交出来——角色、名字、矩形——于是点击 就变成「那个矩形的中心」，什么也不用看。 ```js desktop_control({ action: 'controls', title: '记事本' }) // 4 [Button] '最小化' @ 887,1 45x39 // 14 [Button] '新建会话' @ 12,54 256x24 // 23 [Edit] '搜索会话名称' @ 204,238 4x20 offscreen desktop_control({ action: 'click', target: 14, title: '记事本' }) ``` **控件树不是更快的截图，是另一种取舍。** | | 截图 | 控件树 | | --- | --- | --- | | 读一次 | ~150 ms，~1k token | ~130-300 ms，~850 token（过滤后） | | 点击位置 | 从像素里估 | 控件的精确矩形 | | 状态 | 「看着像禁用」 | `enabled`、`offscreen`、`HasKeyboardFocus`、`IsSelected`、值 | | 可用性 | 永远有 | **不一定有**，见下 | 按单次调用看，树更慢或打平；按单个任务看，树快得多——一次读取能定位好几个目标， 既不用多截一张图，也不用多跑一轮推理。 **它不是总存在。** canvas、绘图面、自绘列表、以及什么都不上报的 Electron 窗口， 给出的树要么是空的要么没意义。所以截图这条路还在，而且仍然是兜底：先读树， 树为空、或者你需要看「画出来什么」而不是「声明了什么」时，再截一张图。 **三个要知道的点。** - 索引只针对「某一次列表」。点击时会重新读一遍再解析，而且暖 worker 记着它发出去的 那份列表，所以某一行换了身份会明确报错，而不是按位置点下去： `the control at index 4 is not the one that was listed: expected [Button] 'OK', found [Button] 'Cancel'`。 - `meaningfulOnly`（默认 `true`）只返回人能操作的控件。在一个真实的 673 元素窗口上， 这是 77 个元素、约 850 token，而不是 9k——其余全是没名字、没状态、点了也没反应的 布局面板。要整棵树就传 `false`。 - `includeValues` 默认关闭：结构不是内容。即使打开，密码框也会被打码。 **当你要找的东西本身没有树**——聊天记录、画布、自绘面板——不要去找它。去找围着它的 东西再做减法：输入框是个带矩形的 `Edit`，窗口有矩形，那么聊天区就是它们之间剩下的那块。 或者干脆不用几何：在树里选中那一条，用 `HasKeyboardFocus` 确认键盘落点就是你要的地方， 打字，回车。最后这一步是截图做不到的——截图能给你一根光标，给不了保证。 ## 为什么安全 给模型装上手，最该讲究的就是这一块： - **风险先声明、后强制**：默认 `low` 可自由批量；声明 `medium`/`high` 的批次、或含 `risk: "high"` 步骤的批次，**在碰桌面之前**就被拒绝，除非调用方带 `confirm: true`（而它只会在你同意之后带）。 - **`dryRun: true`** 只校验并列出计划，不执行。 - **默认遇错即停**：`focus` 失败绝不会有"接着往面前那个窗口里打字"的后续。 - **定向输入**：步骤里指定了窗口（`hwnd`）时，注入前会再次把该窗口置前，点击不会落进旁边的窗口。 - **结果不明就绝不静默重试**：worker 在请求送达后死掉时，动作按失败上报而不是重放——它可能已经生效了；截图没有副作用，才会自动回退重试。 - **中断是真的能中断**：按 Esc 会写取消令牌，动作循环在每一步之间轮询（拖拽中、等待中、截图前都查），拖拽在 `finally` 里松开按键——中断的回合不会留下按住的鼠标，也不会把剩下的点击跑完。 - **不会假装成功**：Windows 禁止向更高完整性级别（提权）的窗口注入输入，工具会如实报错。 - **批量有上限**：`maxSequenceSteps`（默认 24）。 ## 安装 ```powershell # 从 npm 装（推荐） dsh plugin --profile <你的profile> add @momasiku/dsh-pilot # 或从仓库装 dsh plugin --profile <你的profile> add github:momasiku/dsh-pilot # 或用本仓库 Release 里的预构建包，免构建授权 dsh plugin --profile <你的profile> add https://github.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot/releases/latest/download/dsh-pilot.tgz # 或你本地已有的检出 dsh plugin --profile <你的profile> add "file:E:\path\to\dsh-pilot" ``` **下载：** [npm 包](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@momasiku/dsh-pilot) · [预构建 tarball](https://github.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot/releases/latest/download/dsh-pilot.tgz) · [源码](https://github.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot) ✅ **推荐用 npm 上的 scoped 包名 `@momasiku/dsh-pilot`。** 裸名 `dsh-pilot` 在 npm 上属于另一款无关的浏览器操控插件，而 `dsh plugin add` 总是先查 npm，所以别用裸名；用仓库地址或 tarball 也照样可以。 包**自带 loader 行**：`plugin add` 会把 `@momasiku/dsh-pilot` 放进 `dsh.profile.bundles`，行本身来自包内的 `cordis.patch.yml`（由 `dsh.bundle.patch` 声明），所以不会像手写补丁行那样被插件管理器重写时弄丢。装完**重启一次 DSH Desktop**，然后**新开一个会话**，三个工具就会出现在工具列表里。 要求 DSH **0.1.5-rc.2 至 0.2.x**（即 `package.json` 里的 peer 范围，也是 `dsh plugin add` 在安装前的门禁）。环境要求：**Windows**、PowerShell 5.1 或 7、以及声明了图像输入的模型线路（`deepseek-flash` 可以）。 ### 最近改动 **0.7.0** —— 浮层重做：一圈淡光、一块读得清的提示牌，以及「截图里不该有它」。 - **屏幕四边一圈天蓝渐变光**（四条带，各自一条 `LinearGradientBrush`，无描边，峰值 alpha 110）。发光只到边缘、向内 56px 淡出，所以看起来是光渗进来，不是一个画上去的框。 - **顶部提示变成一块蓝色半透明面板**：圆角 20、`rgba(18,74,148,140)`，边框上一段高光**绕圈跑**（旋转渐变），字体换成 Segoe UI / 微软雅黑 **SemiBold**，`Esc` 做成真正的键帽。 - **去掉光标光晕**。它只能靠轮询 `GetCursorPos` 再移动窗口，无论循环多快都会慢一两帧 —— 一个总是慢半拍的影子光标比没有更糟。 - **截图前自动让开**：宿主写 `mute.txt`，等浮层回 `muted.txt`（≤180 ms）再截，拍完立刻恢复。现在 `screen_view` 出来的图是干净的，没有一个亮边压在画面上。 - **单实例的洞补上了**：互斥名是按 `StateDir` **字符串**算的，`C:\Users\Administrator\…` 和 `C:\Users\ADMINI~1\…` 指向同一目录却是两个名字，于是两个浮层会同时画。现在多一个 `instance.txt` 的 PID 锁，跟路径写法无关。 - **刷新 33 ms → 16 ms**（光晕没了之后额外开销很小），呼吸每 8 帧应用一次，分辨率每秒检查一次：阿里云这类会话中途改分辨率，面板不会再被推出屏幕。 - **tick 里的异常不再静默**：以前抛错会被 dispatcher 吞掉，浮层停在屏幕上但完全不动；现在 catch 住并写进 `status.txt`。 - `overlay-smoke` 的首帧门槛从 2000 ms 调到 3000 ms：这台负载机光 PowerShell 启动就要 1.8–2.1 s，0.6.5 原版实测 1874 ms。 **0.6.5** —— 接管提示终于看得见：像素对了，停留时间也能调。 - **浮层没声明 DPI 感知**，150% 缩放下它以为屏幕是 1707×1067（实际 2560×1600）：顶部文字被放大半倍，跟随鼠标的光环画到别处去了。现在在加载 WPF **之前**声明 per-monitor v2，按真实像素排版，光环落在指针上。 - **隐藏延迟从写死的 2 秒变成配置项** `takeoverLingerMs`，默认 **8 秒**：单步动作也来得及看清是谁在操作，Esc 仍然随时能取消。 - 浮层脚本里“宿主两秒后隐藏”的注释同步改成引用这个配置项。 **0.6.4** —— 接管提示改成按回合显示。 - **以前每个动作开关一次，画图这种连续操作就是一路闪。** 现在一个回合只显示一次，**最后一次动作后 2 秒**才隐藏；新动作会取消这个隐藏。 - **首次出画约 0.7 秒**（不预热）。比这更短的单步动作仍然可能看不到第一帧 —— 这是不预热的代价。 - **修掉启动竞态**：脚本末尾的 `Show()`/`Hide()` 会和定时器的第一次真实显示撞车，导致首个动作记两次 show。句柄已经由 `EnsureHandle()` 建好，那两句是多余的。 - **`Test-Path` 短暂失败不再立即隐藏**：宿主每次动作都会截断重写 `show.txt`，正好撞上读不到就是一次假隐藏。现在连续三次读不到才隐藏。 - **单实例互斥**：一个进程独占一个状态目录，DSH 重启留下的孤儿不会再和新进程抢同一块屏幕。 - **新增 `tools/overlay-smoke.ps1`**：首次出画耗时、回合内不重显、结束只隐藏一次、第二份进程必须退出。 **0.6.3** —— `controls` 的两处真问题（issue #1 / #2）。 - **结构化输出里有、模型可见文本里没有**：`controlText()` 只拼了 action / cursor / foreground，把 `controls` 和 `windows` 整个丢了 —— 对纯文本模型来说，README 里说的「便宜路径」事实上不可用，只能退回截图。现在渲染成 `` / `` 块，并带上窗口名与计数。 - **`meaningfulOnly` 的 `$name` 从未赋值**：`$null.Length -eq 0` 恒为真，于是 ListItem / TreeItem / MenuItem / DataItem 四类**无论有没有名字都被丢弃**。改成读元素自己的名字，与注释里写的意图一致。 - **`Pane` 不在白名单**：原生 Win32 对话框（`#32770`）的所有子控件经 MSAA 桥接后都报 `Pane`，于是一个满是按钮的对话框过滤后是空的。命名 Pane 现在算控件，无名 Pane 仍视作布局。 - **过滤不再无声**：新增 `controlTotal` / `filteredOut` 并渲染进文本。实测「运行」对话框：10 个元素，保留 6 个（确定 / 取消 / 浏览 / 提示文字），丢掉 4 个无名 Pane。 - **回归测试**：`script-smoke` 现在会真按一次 `Win+R`，断言该对话框在 `meaningfulOnly:true` 下非空且含「确定/取消」，随后 Esc 关闭。 **0.6.2** —— 兼容性声明落到能验证的地方。 - **在 DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 上实测通过**：`screen_view` 抓屏、`windows` 枚举、`controls` 控件树、`desktop_sequence` 三步批次都正常，peer 声明 `>=0.2.1-0 <0.3.0-0` 本身就覆盖 rc.3。 - **`check-peers` 新增 `--asar`**：以前它只校验开发副本 `node_modules`（可能落在旧代），现在可以直接读**已安装桌面端**的 `app.asar`，按里面真实携带的 dsh-* 版本判定 —— 也就是用户真正在跑的那一代。 - **`--asar` 的两个细节**：Electron 的 fs 会把 `.asar` 当压缩包拦截，读取失败时回退到临时副本；asar 头部按 4 字节对齐填充 NUL，要剥掉尾部才能 `JSON.parse`。 **0.6.1** —— 简介和 README 都用中文先说。 - **仓库简介和 npm 简介换成同一句中文**：能做和人一样的事，包括且不仅限于 CAD、WPS、浏览器操作、发微信；安全、快速、可靠、聪明、人性化。 - **中文说明移到 README 顶部**，英文段落后置并加上 `# English` 标题，顶部语言链接同步调换。 - 没有代码改动。 **0.5.14** —— 坐标契约不再猜「你看到的那张图有多大」。 - **请求管线会在抓取之后再缩一次**，而插件看不到这一步：2560×1600 的屏幕上，帧送到模型时是 1610×1006，契约却写着「交付即抓取尺寸……不要缩放」，于是每个读数都偏 1.59 倍。现在契约用部署公布的图片预算**预测**投影尺寸，并把尺寸和乘数一起写出来：`2560x1600 抓取 → 1609x1006 预览，把每个读数乘 1.5911`。面积落在预算内的帧会原样送达，所以抓窗口或抓区域能得到真正的 1:1 —— 1365×960 可以，1024×768 可以；4K 和 5K 则分别写 2.2642 倍和 3.0189 倍。 **0.5.12** —— 冷树，以及一个什么都没说的空列表。 - **Chromium 的无障碍树是懒加载的**，而且由第一个来问的人付账：实测重启后在 1.2 秒时只有 3 个元素，下一次调用 0.3 秒时是 77 个。信任第一个答案的人会认定「这窗口没有树」，白白退回像素。现在 `controls` 在「worker 还没见过完整树、且结果异常少」时会等 300 ms 重试一次。 - **过滤后确实什么都没匹配到时，现在会明说**，而不是返回一个读起来像「这里没有树」的空列表：`(no operable controls here; the window has 2 elements - pass meaningfulOnly:false to see them)`。 **0.5.11** —— 控件树，外加两个让批量操作「不说谎」的修复。 - **`controls` 读窗口的 UI Automation 树**，`target` 点列表里那个控件的精确矩形，于是有名字的控件不必再去像素里找。它不截图，所以也不付 settle。在 673 个元素的窗口上实测：过滤后 **0.65 秒、约 850 token**（77 个可操作元素），不过滤约 9k。暖 worker 记着它发出去的那份列表，所以某一行换了身份会报错，而不是点到搬进来的那个。 - **不截图的动作也在付 settle**（0.5.9）。settle 本是为了「别在重绘中途取帧」，但 `desktop_control` 每次调用都付。实测不截图的动作用时 **814 ms → 12 ms**。 - **`focus` 被拒绝却报成功**（0.5.9）。那一步只记一条备注、仍然说 `ok`，于是批量剩下的步骤全打进了真正在前台的那个窗口。现在改成在尝试之后检查真实前台——看状态，不看 `SetForegroundWindow` 的返回值——不符就报错并说出两个窗口。`tolerant: true` 可以恢复旧行为，给「坐标反正都对」的调用方留口子。 - **peer 范围开始接受 0.2.1 世代**（0.5.10）。`0.2.1` 这个元组需要它自己的预发布比较符：预发布版本只有在某个比较符与它同属一个 `major.minor.patch`、且自身带预发布标签时才放行。 **0.5.8** —— 两个修复，同时包已发布到 npm：[`@momasiku/dsh-pilot`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@momasiku/dsh-pilot)。 - **显示器几何会变陈旧，而且是静默的。** 原本显示器清单来自 `System.Windows.Forms.Screen.AllScreens`，这是静态缓存，只有进程处理 `WM_DISPLAYCHANGE` 时才刷新；而暖 worker 是没有消息泵的 `-NonInteractive` 读取循环，缓存永远不会失效。实测：存活 13 小时的 worker 报 `primary WinDisc 0,0,1600,900`，而同一份结果里的 `` 是 `1024x768` —— 同一份结果两个答案，而坐标契约正是从这份帧里读的。现在每次截图都用 `EnumDisplayMonitors` 重新枚举，虚拟屏改用 `GetSystemMetrics`，两者都不缓存。 - **冷启动每次都重付编译开销。** Win32 桥原本每次进程启动都要 `Add-Type` 编译一次，而且发生在 worker 能回答 `ready` 之前 —— 正是暖 worker 存在的意义所在的那笔开销。现在按源码哈希编译一次存成 DLL，之后直接加载。一次性抓帧 **2638 ms → 813 ms**，暖动作仍是 **9 ms**。改源码会换哈希、换 DLL，缓存绝不会遮蔽后续修复。 npm 上的包名带 scope，是因为 `dsh-pilot` 这个名字在 npm 上属于另一款无关的浏览器操控插件。**仓库名仍然是 `momasiku/dsh-pilot`。** ## 使用要点 - 先 `desktop_control { action: "windows" }` 看清有哪些窗口、哪个在前台，再动手。 - 多步任务优先用 `desktop_sequence`：把"聚焦 → 点击 → 输入 → 回车"写成一次调用。 - 打字支持多行与中文（走剪贴板一次粘贴，之后恢复剪贴板）。 - 想更省 token：`capture: "none"` 不附图，或依赖"未变化不重发"；想看得更清：`rulers: true`（默认开）。 - 常用设置（`captureRetention`、`settleMs`、`stepSettleMs`、`maxSequenceSteps`、`useWorker`、`rulers`）写在配置行里，见上面的 Settings 一节。 ## 常见问题 | 现象 | 原因与处理 | | --- | --- | | 提示找不到匹配窗口 | 窗口缩到托盘了，或标题变了：用 `action: "windows"` 列出来，或改用 `hwnd` 指定 | | 点击总是差一点 | 图片被宿主压小了：看 `` 的乘数并乘上去 | | 点了没反应 | 目标窗口可能是提权窗口，Windows 不允许跨完整性级别注入输入 | | 升级后工具不见了 | 重启 DSH Desktop：包的代码在加载时重新导入，profile 的插件行在启动时合成 | | 批次被拒绝执行 | 声明了 `medium`/`high`：经用户同意后带 `confirm: true` 重发，或先用 `dryRun: true` 看计划 | ## License MIT © 2026 momasiku --- # English > **Windows desktop control.** The model sees the real screen and drives the real > mouse and keyboard. Out of the box, a DeepSeek Harness session can reason about your desktop but cannot touch it: you describe what is on screen, you take the screenshots, you do the clicking, and you report what happened. **dsh-pilot closes that loop.** The model looks at the real pixels and then operates them: ### Demos ![dsh-pilot drawing a mechanical plate in AutoCAD: the model types REC and the corner coordinates, the inner outline, five circles, the centre lines and two linear dimensions into the command line, then zooms to extents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot/main/assets/dsh-pilot-cad.gif) **A CAD drawing, drawn by the model.** It drives AutoCAD's own command line — `REC` → `0,0` → `240,150`, the inner outline, five holes, centre lines and two dimensions — and installs nothing inside AutoCAD. ![dsh-pilot renaming a column in LibreOffice Calc: focus the workbook, move the pointer to C1, click, paste "Q3 收入", press Enter, Ctrl+S — all in one desktop_sequence call](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot/main/assets/dsh-pilot-excel.gif) **A spreadsheet edit, in one call.** `desktop_sequence` focuses the workbook, moves the pointer to C1, clicks, pastes `Q3 收入`, presses Enter and saves — one round trip for the whole chain. ![dsh-pilot modelling in Blender: the viewport is cleared, a cube is added, and subdivision turns it into a sphere, then the model orbits to check it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot/main/assets/dsh-pilot-blender.gif) **A 3D model, built from nothing.** It clears the viewport, adds a cube, then `Ctrl+1` and `Ctrl+3` subdivision turn that cube into a sphere. Real Blender 4.2 on a machine with **no GPU** — driven through Mesa's software OpenGL, which the model set up itself. | tool | what it does | | --- | --- | | **`screen_view`** | captures the live desktop and returns the PNG as a **real image block** the model can see — not OCR, not a text summary | | **`desktop_control`** | moves the pointer, clicks, drags, scrolls, types, sends keys, focuses and lists windows — and can capture the result in the same call | | **`desktop_sequence`** | runs a **whole batch** of those actions in one call and looks once at the end | ## Why this exists A model that cannot see the screen has to be told what is on it. A model that cannot touch the screen has to be told what to do next. That turns every desktop task into a conversation about the desktop instead of work on the desktop — and the user becomes the hands, the eyes, and the error message. The expensive part of desktop automation was never the mouse. It is **how many times the model and the computer have to talk**: | a five-step task: focus a window, click a field, type, press Enter, look at the result | DSH alone | DSH + dsh-pilot | | --- | --- | --- | | who reads the screen | you | the model, from real pixels | | who clicks and types | you | the model | | model ↔ computer round trips | 5 (one per step, plus yours) | **1** | | screenshots shipped to the model | 4–5 | **1** | | where the model spends its time | waiting, re-describing, re-asking | thinking about the task | | when a step fails | you notice | the same result says which step, and why | ## What it feels like ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as You participant M as Model participant P as dsh-pilot participant W as Warm worker (PowerShell) participant D as Your desktop U->>M: 把第三列改名成 Q3 收入并保存 M->>P: screen_view(window: "报表") P->>D: capture (per-monitor DPI aware) D-->>M: real PNG + cursor, foreground window, monitor bounds M->>P: desktop_sequence([focus, click, type, key, key]) P->>W: 5 requests over one pipe — 6–12 ms each W->>D: SetCursorPos, SendInput, clipboard paste D-->>M: one end frame (with coordinate rulers) + per-step outcome ``` ## Why the coordinates can be trusted The classic way a vision-driven click goes wrong is a coordinate that is *almost* right. dsh-pilot removes the three ways that happens: **1. Both halves are per-monitor DPI aware.** A DPI-unaware process is lied to by Windows: it sees a 2560×1600 panel as 1707×1067, so every click computed from such a screenshot lands in the wrong place. The sensor and the effector each declare `SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext(PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2)` before doing anything, so one image pixel is one physical screen pixel. **2. Frames carry rulers.** Ticks every 200 px along the top and left edge, each labelled with the **screen coordinate** it sits at, plus an `origin x,y step n` note. The model reads a position off the image instead of counting pixels — and because the labels are screen coordinates, they survive any downscaling the attachment store does. **3. The envelope says what it actually delivered.** If the store re-encodes a frame smaller, the model is told the ratio and the multiplier, and the coordinate contract becomes conditional — it only promises "use x and y as they are" when the delivered frame *is* the capture: ```text 1974x873 delivered 1974x873 = 0.873x capture; multiply image readings by 1.1454 to get screen pixels ``` ## Why it is fast Batching is the big win (round trips, not clicks). The second win is that PowerShell stops being restarted: one warm worker process answers every action and every frame. | request | one-shot script | warm worker | | --- | --- | --- | | action (`move`, `click`, `type`, …) | ~0.9–2.0 s | **6–12 ms** | | capture (primary monitor) | ~1.2–2.3 s | **~0.5 s** | Measured on a 2560×1600 panel at 150% scaling with the harness UI animating. The worker is started in the background on the first tool call, so the ~1 s it needs overlaps the first capture instead of delaying the first action. **Identical frames are not resent.** Every capture returns a `frameHash`; when a frame is byte-identical to the previous one of the same session, the image is not attached (or stored) again — the result says `unchanged: true` and the coordinates from the frame the model already has still apply. `forceImage: true` overrides it. ## Reading the control tree A screenshot costs a guess: the model finds a button in pixels, estimates its centre, clicks, and takes another frame to see whether the guess was right. Windows exposes the same control through UI Automation as a role, a name and a rectangle, so the click becomes the centre of that rectangle and nothing has to be looked at. ```js desktop_control({ action: 'controls', title: 'Notepad' }) // 4 [Button] '最小化' @ 887,1 45x39 // 14 [Button] '新建会话' @ 12,54 256x24 // 23 [Edit] '搜索会话名称' @ 204,238 4x20 offscreen desktop_control({ action: 'click', target: 14, title: 'Notepad' }) ``` **The tree is not a faster screenshot; it is a different trade.** | | screenshot | control tree | | --- | --- | --- | | one read | ~150 ms, ~1k tokens | ~130-300 ms, ~850 tokens (filtered) | | click target | estimated from pixels | the control's exact rectangle | | state | "looks disabled" | `enabled`, `offscreen`, `HasKeyboardFocus`, `IsSelected`, value | | availability | always | **not always** - see below | Per call the tree is slower or level. Per task it is much faster, because one read resolves several targets without another frame and without another round trip. **It does not always exist.** A canvas, a drawing surface, a custom-painted list and an Electron window that publishes nothing all give an empty or useless tree. That is why the screenshot path is still there and still the fallback: read the tree first, take a frame when the tree is empty or when you need to see what is drawn rather than what is declared. **Three things worth knowing.** - An index addresses one row of one listing. It is resolved against a fresh read at click time, and the worker remembers the listing it handed out, so a row that changed identity fails loudly instead of being clicked by position: `the control at index 4 is not the one that was listed: expected [Button] 'OK', found [Button] 'Cancel'`. - `meaningfulOnly` (default `true`) returns only the roles a person can operate. On a real 673-element window that is 77 elements and ~850 tokens instead of 9k - the rest is layout panes with no name, no state and nothing to click. Pass `false` for the whole tree. - `includeValues` is off by default: structure is not content. Password fields are masked even when it is on. **When the thing you want has no tree of its own** - a chat transcript, a canvas, a custom-painted panel - do not look for it. Look for what surrounds it and subtract: the composer is an `Edit` with a rectangle, the window has a rectangle, so the transcript is what is left between them. Or skip the geometry: select the item in the tree, confirm with `HasKeyboardFocus` that the keyboard is where you want it, type, press Enter. That last step is something a screenshot cannot do - it can show a caret, not a promise. ## Why it is safe Giving a model hands is the part worth getting right: - **Risk is declared, then enforced.** Low risk (default) batches freely. A batch declared `medium`/`high`, or one carrying a step marked `risk: "high"`, is refused *before anything touches the desktop* unless the caller passes `confirm: true` — which it does only after you agreed. - **`dryRun: true`** validates a batch and lists the plan without executing. - **Stop on the first failure** (default): a refused `focus` can never be followed by typing into whatever window happens to be in front. - **Targeted input.** When a step names a window (`hwnd`), the effector re-asserts it as foreground immediately before injecting, so a click cannot land in a neighbour. - **An unknown outcome is never a silent retry.** If the worker dies after a request was delivered, the action is reported as failed rather than repeated — it may already have taken effect. A capture has no side effects, so it *is* retried. - **Interruption works.** Pressing Esc writes a cancel token, the action loop polls it between every step (during drags, during the settle wait, before the capture) and a drag releases the button in a `finally` block, so an aborted turn cannot leave the mouse latched down or the remaining clicks playing out. - **It cannot lie about privilege.** Windows refuses input injection into a higher-integrity (elevated) window; the tool reports that failure instead of pretending it worked. - **`desktop_sequence` is bounded** by `maxSequenceSteps` (default 24). ## Install ```powershell # from npm (recommended) dsh plugin --profile add @momasiku/dsh-pilot # or from the repository dsh plugin --profile add github:momasiku/dsh-pilot # or this repository's prebuilt tarball, which skips the build-approval step dsh plugin --profile add https://github.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot/releases/latest/download/dsh-pilot.tgz # or a checkout you already have dsh plugin --profile add "file:E:\path\to\dsh-pilot" ``` **Download:** [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@momasiku/dsh-pilot) · [prebuilt tarball](https://github.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot/releases/latest/download/dsh-pilot.tgz) · [source](https://github.com/momasiku/dsh-pilot) **Install by the scoped name.** `dsh plugin add` asks the npm registry first, and the unscoped name `dsh-pilot` on npm belongs to an unrelated browser-automation plugin - so install as `@momasiku/dsh-pilot`, or by repository / tarball as shown above. The package ships its own loader row, so `plugin add` places `@momasiku/dsh-pilot` in `dsh.profile.bundles` and the row comes from the package (`dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`) rather than being hand-written into your patch layer. **Restart the desktop app** once afterwards, then start a new conversation: the three tools join the tool list. Requires DSH **0.1.5-rc.2 through 0.2.x** — that is the peer range in `package.json`, and what `dsh plugin add` checks before it installs anything. Requirements: **Windows**, PowerShell 5.1 or 7, and a model route that declares image input (`deepseek-flash` does). ### Recent changes **0.6.5** — the takeover prompt is finally visible: right pixels, and a linger you can see. - **The overlay declared no DPI awareness**, so at 150% it laid itself out for a 1707×1067 screen instead of 2560×1600: the caption came out half again too large and the cursor halo was drawn away from the pointer. It now declares per-monitor v2 before WPF loads and lays out in real pixels, so the halo sits on the pointer. - **The hide delay is a setting now** (`takeoverLingerMs`, default **8 s**) instead of a hard-coded two seconds: a single action is long enough to read, and Esc still cancels at any time. - The comment in the overlay script about the host's two-second linger now names the setting. **0.6.4** — the takeover prompt is held per round, not per action. - **It used to toggle on every action, so a run of small steps strobed.** One round now shows it once and hides it **two seconds after the last action**; a new action cancels that hide. - **First paint takes about 0.7 s** (no pre-warm, by request). A single action shorter than that can still miss the first frame - that is the price of not pre-warming. - **Fixed a startup race**: the `Show()`/`Hide()` at the end of the script collided with the timer's first real show, logging two shows for the first action. The handles already exist from `EnsureHandle()`, so those two lines were redundant. - **A transient `Test-Path` failure no longer hides the overlay**: the host rewrites `show.txt` with a truncating write on every action, and a check that lands in that window reads false. It now takes three consecutive misses. - **Single instance**: one process owns a state directory, so an overlay orphaned by a host restart cannot fight the new one for the same screen. - **New `tools/overlay-smoke.ps1`**: first-paint latency, no re-show inside a round, exactly one hide at the end, and a second copy must exit. **0.6.3** — two real `controls` bugs, both reported in issues #1 and #2. - **Structured output had them, the model's text did not**: `controlText()` only wrote action / cursor / foreground, dropping `controls` and `windows` entirely — so the "cheap path" the README describes was unusable for a text-only model, which fell back to screenshots. Both now render as `` / `` blocks, with the window name and counts. - **`meaningfulOnly` compared an unassigned `$name`**: `$null.Length -eq 0` is always true, so ListItem, TreeItem, MenuItem and DataItem rows were dropped whether they had a name or not. It reads the element's own name now, which is what the comment above it always said. - **`Pane` was missing from the whitelist**: every child of a native Win32 dialog (`#32770`) bridges through MSAA and reports as a Pane, so a dialog full of buttons filtered down to nothing. A named Pane now counts as a control; an unnamed one is still layout. - **Filtering is no longer silent**: `controlTotal` and `filteredOut` are new, and they render into the text. Measured on the Run dialog: 10 elements, 6 kept (OK / Cancel / Browse / the prompt), 4 unnamed Panes dropped. - **Regression test**: `script-smoke` now raises a real `Win+R` dialog, asserts it is non-empty under `meaningfulOnly: true` and contains OK/Cancel, then closes it with Esc. **0.6.2** — the compatibility claim now sits where it can be checked. - **Verified on DSH 0.2.1-rc.3**: `screen_view`, `windows`, `controls` and a three-step `desktop_sequence` all ran there, and the declared peer range `>=0.2.1-0 <0.3.0-0` already covered rc.3. - **`check-peers --asar`**: the check used to judge only the dev copy in `node_modules`, which can sit on an older generation than the app a user actually runs. It now reads the installed desktop app's `app.asar` and judges against the dsh-* versions that build really carries. - **Two details the flag had to handle**: Electron's patched fs treats any `.asar` path as an archive and refuses the bytes, so a failed read falls back to a temporary copy; and the asar header is NUL-padded to a four-byte boundary, so the padding has to go before `JSON.parse`. **0.6.1** — the description and the README lead with Chinese. - **The repository and npm descriptions are now the same Chinese sentence**: the things a person can do — CAD, WPS, a browser, WeChat — and safe, fast, reliable, smart, humane. - **The Chinese section moved to the top of the README**; the English one follows under a `# English` heading, and the language links at the top were swapped. - No code changed. **0.6.0** — a takeover line, a lit pointer, and titles that stop hiding characters. - **The screen says who is driving.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-balance

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) web
plugin that shows your **real DeepSeek account balance** and the **current
peak/off-peak pricing window** in a window-anchored card, and estimates the
**cost of every conversation and workspace** from the session log.

![Balance card and detail panel](screenshot.png)

## Features

- **Balance card** — fixed to the bottom-right of the window, independent of the
  composer: live account balance, current window (`谷价` / `高峰`), remaining
  time, and the next switch in your local timezone. It stays at the window
  bottom even on the no-conversation/hero screen, and moves above the composer
  or the per-conversation status row when they reach that corner, so it never
  covers other readings.
- **Native detail panel** — click the card to open a menu-style panel above it:
  account balance / topped-up / granted, next switch in local and Beijing time,
  current local/Beijing time, peak hours, price-table source and update time,
  ledger path, and a refresh button. Closes on outside click or `Esc`.
- **Cost estimates** — per-conversation and per-workspace estimates in the
  sidebar, summed from a persistent ledger that records each usage event once.
- **Dynamic pricing** — CNY and USD price tables and the peak-hour windows are
  fetched from the official DeepSeek pricing pages; the Chinese holiday calendar
  comes from `api.apihubs.cn`.
- **Theme and language aware** — uses the DSH menu-surface design tokens
  (light/dark, radius, type scale), follows the DSH UI language
  (`zh-*` / English).
- **Peak-switch notifications** — optional browser notification when the window
  changes, only if notification permission was already granted for the DSH site.

## Requirements

- **DSH 0.2.1.x** with the web profile. Tested with `0.2.1-rc.3`; the package
  declares `engines.dsh = ">=0.2.1-0 <0.2.2-0"` and DSH refuses to mount it on
  other lines.
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the DSH requirement).
- A DeepSeek API key configured in DSH's credentials as `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`.

## Install

Install this repository directly from GitHub:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:zz0-0/dsh-balance
systemctl --user restart dsh-web
```

Or with an explicit git URL:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/zz0-0/dsh-balance.git
systemctl --user restart dsh-web
```

Then **hard-refresh** the DSH web page (`Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + R`). The plugin
injects its browser script into the DSH index page, so the refresh is needed the
first time. The `systemctl` line assumes the Linux user service; if you run
`dsh web` manually, restart that process instead.

> **Not the npm package.** The npm package named `dsh-balance` is an unrelated
> project by another author. Install this plugin with the GitHub coordinate
> above, not with `dsh plugin add dsh-balance`.

### Update

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:zz0-0/dsh-balance
systemctl --user restart dsh-web
```

### Remove

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-balance
systemctl --user restart dsh-web
```

## Usage

Click the balance card in the bottom-right corner to open the detail panel.
The card itself shows the total balance, the current pricing window, the
countdown to the next switch, and that switch time in your local zone.

The sidebar shows an `≈¥…` estimate on each conversation row and the sum of its
conversations on each workspace row. Hovering a badge shows its tokens and the
recorded estimate.

There is deliberately **no cost pill in the composer status row**: that row is
per-conversation and gets crowded quickly, and the conversation row already
carries the estimate.

If notification permission was granted for the DSH site, the browser notifies
when the peak/off-peak window changes while the DSH tab is open. A fully closed
browser cannot receive notifications.

## Pricing and the ledger

### Pricing is fetched, not hardcoded

At startup and whenever the cached table is older than six hours, the host
fetches both official pricing pages:

| Currency | Page |
|---|---|
| CNY | `https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing` |
| USD | `https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing` |

The parser reads the model pricing table dynamically, including the model
columns, cache-hit/cache-miss/output prices, and the peak-hour windows from the
Chinese page footnote. If a page changes shape and parsing fails, the previous
cache is kept and the detail panel marks the source as `缓存/默认`
(`cache/default`).

### Peak windows

Peak is Beijing weekday **09:00–12:00** and **14:00–18:00**. Weekends are
always off-peak (from 2026-08-23), and a weekday marked as a public holiday is
off-peak. A make-up weekend is still a weekend, so it is off-peak.

The holiday calendar is fetched from:

```
https://api.apihubs.cn/holiday/get?year=YYYY&size=500
```

for the current and next year, and cached for 30 days.

### The ledger never reprices old spend

The cost ledger is `~/.dsh/.dsh-balance-costs.json`. Each session entry stores:

- `costs.CNY` and `costs.USD`
- `tokens`
- `lastSeq` — the last event already recorded
- `pricingVersions` — price snapshots used for its recorded events
- `calendarVersions` — holiday calendars used for its recorded events

When a session is scanned again, only events with `seq > lastSeq` are priced.
Already-recorded events are never recalculated, so a price change affects only
**new** events and a restart cannot rewrite what was already spent.

### Currency

`/user/balance` can return multiple `balance_infos`. The plugin stores costs in
both CNY and USD, then displays the bucket for the primary account currency: the
**largest non-zero balance** returned by the API (CNY wins a tie). If both
currencies have a positive balance, the card shows both stacked while estimates
use the larger one. A USD-only account uses the USD pricing table and `$`
badges.

## How it works

The plugin is a DSH bundle: `package.json` declares
`dsh.bundle.patch = ./cordis.patch.yml`, and that patch inserts the
`dsh-balance` entry into the web profile. It has two halves:

| Half | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Host | `lib/index.js` | Resolves `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` through DSH credentials, queries `/user/balance`, reads session events, keeps the ledger, fetches prices/holidays, serves `GET /dsh-balance/data` and `GET /dsh-balance/client.js`. |
| Browser | `client.js` | Injected into the DSH index page. Draws the balance card and detail panel, and adds cost badges to conversation/workspace rows. |

The browser only talks to the local DSH server. The API key never reaches the
browser.

Cache files, all under `~/.dsh/` (or `$DSH_HOME`):

- `.dsh-balance-costs.json` — the cost ledger
- `.dsh-balance-pricing.json` — current price table and peak hours
- `.dsh-balance-pricing-history.json` — one entry per changed price snapshot
- `.dsh-balance-holidays.json` — current holiday calendar

## Privacy

- **Outbound requests**: `api.deepseek.com/user/balance` (with your API key),
  the two DeepSeek pricing pages, and `api.apihubs.cn/holiday/get`. Nothing
  else, and no telemetry.
- **Local-only**: the ledger and caches stay in `~/.dsh/`. The browser only
  requests `/dsh-balance/data` from your local DSH server.
- **Credential handling**: the key is resolved host-side through DSH's
  credentials service and is never serialized into the browser payload.

## Troubleshooting

- **Card shows `余额?` / `Balance?`** — `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is missing or invalid;
  check DSH's credentials configuration and the host log.
- **Price source says `缓存/默认`** — the pricing page could not be fetched or
  parsed; the last cached table is still used.
- **No notifications** — permission was not granted for the DSH site, or the tab
  is closed.
- **Plugin not visible after install** — restart the `dsh web` process and
  hard-refresh the browser. Verify the profile lists the plugin.
- **Install refused with an incompatible-version error** — the package declares
  `engines.dsh` for the DSH 0.2.1 line only.

## Development

The plugin has no build step: plain ESM on the host and a classic browser script.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zz0-0/dsh-balance.git
cd dsh-balance
dsh plugin --profile web add link:$(pwd)
systemctl --user restart dsh-web
```

- `client.js` is served with `Cache-Control: no-store`. With a `link:` install,
  edit and hard-refresh the browser.
- `lib/index.js` is host-side: edit and restart `dsh-web`.
- A git install keeps its own copy under the profile's `node_modules`; after
  editing the checkout, reinstall the plugin (or sync `client.js` into the
  installed package) and refresh.

### Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | DSH bundle metadata and compatibility |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Inserts the plugin into the web profile |
| `lib/index.js` | Host: balance, pricing, holidays, ledger, HTTP routes, client injection |
| `client.js` | Browser: balance card + detail panel, row badges, notifications |
| `screenshot.png` | README screenshot |

### UI integration

The browser side does not patch React. It uses stable attributes exposed by the
workspace sidebar and composer:

- `[data-row-key="session:<sessionId>"]` and `[data-row-key="workspace:<workspaceId>"]`
  for cost badges (re-added by a `MutationObserver` after React re-renders)
- `[data-composer-card]` and `[data-slot="conversation.composer.dock"]` to keep
  the window-anchored card clear of the composer and the status row
